弘治十八年進士登科錄

玉音

弘治十八年三月初八日，禮部尚書臣張昇等於奉天門奏為科舉事：會試天下舉人，取中三百名。本年三月十五日殿試，合請讀卷官及執事等官，少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士劉健等五十四員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Eighteenth Year of Hongzhi (1505)

Imperial Pronouncement

On the eighth day of the third month of the eighteenth year of Hongzhi, your servant Zhang Sheng, Minister of Rites, and others submitted a memorial at Fengtian Gate concerning the civil-service examinations: “At the Metropolitan Examination for provincial graduates from throughout the realm, three hundred candidates were selected. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we request the appointment of fifty-four officials as Readers and other officiating personnel, including Liu Jian, Junior Preceptor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. The distinctions of metropolitan graduate status shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially prescribed by Emperor Taizu Gao. By established practice, three candidates shall be placed in the first class: the first shall receive rank 6b, and the second and third rank 7a, with the distinction ‘metropolitan graduate with honors’ conferred upon them. Those in the second class shall receive rank 7b and the distinction ‘metropolitan graduate.’ Those in the third class shall receive rank 8a and the distinction ‘equivalent to metropolitan graduate.’” The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Readers

Liu Jian held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Special Advancement, Left Pillar of State, and Junior Preceptor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the gengchen year (1460).〕

Ma Wensheng held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, and Junior Preceptor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year (1451).〕

Li Dongyang held the titles Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and served as Minister of Revenue, concurrently Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the jiashen year (1464).〕

Xie Qian held the titles Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and served as Minister of Rites, concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year (1475).〕

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the eighteenth year of Hongzhi (1505), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. His Majesty took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy questions.

On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court robes. That day, the Embroidered Uniform Guard arranged the ceremonial regalia along the vermilion steps and within the vermilion courtyard. His Majesty took his seat in Fengtian Hall. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and proclaimed the candidates’ names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites respectfully carried the yellow results list out through Chang’an Left Gate, led by drums and music. After the list had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the nineteenth day of the third month…

顧鼎臣〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字九和，行三，年三十三，二月二十五日生〕。曾祖大本，祖良，父恂〔遇例壽官〕；嫡母吳氏，生母楊氏。具慶下。兄式〔府經歷〕、宜之〔封監察御史〕。娶朱氏。應天府鄉試第八十六名，會試第五十五名。

董玘〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字文玉，行十六，年二十三，八月十七日生〕。曾祖孚言，祖敬〔贈監察御史〕，父復〔知府〕；前母章氏〔贈孺人〕，母婁氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下。兄冕、旒，弟軾、龍。聘潘氏。浙江鄉試第二名，會試第一名。

謝丕〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字以中，行三，年二十四，四月十八日生〕。曾祖瑩〔布政司都事，贈太子少保、兵部尚書兼東閣大學士〕，祖恩〔封右諭德，贈太子少保、兵部尚書兼東閣大學士〕，父遷；母陸氏〔旌表節婦〕。慈侍下。兄正，弟豆、亘。娶毛氏。順天府鄉試第一名，會試第四名。
translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the degree of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Gu Dingchen 顧鼎臣 was registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Jiuhe and ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-three sui, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daben, his grandfather Liang, and his father Xun, who received an honorary official title for longevity under the applicable regulations. His legal mother was née Wu and his birth mother née Yang; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shi, a prefectural Registrar, and Yizhi, who was granted the title of Investigating Censor. He married a woman née Zhu. He ranked eighty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Qi 董玘 was registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Wenyu and ranked sixteenth among his brothers. He was twenty-three sui, born on the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuyan, his grandfather Jing, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor, and his father Fu, a Prefect. His father's former wife, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren); his mother, née Lou, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mian and Liu, and his younger brothers Shi and Long. He was betrothed to a woman née Pan. He ranked second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Pi 謝丕 was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Yizhong and ranked third among his brothers. He was twenty-four sui, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ying was an Assistant Office Manager in a Provincial Administration Commission, posthumously granted the titles of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of War, and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Hall. His grandfather En was granted the title of Right Admonisher and posthumously granted the titles of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of War, and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Hall. His father was Qian; his mother, née Lu, received official recognition as a chaste widow. He is recorded as serving his surviving mother. His elder brother was Zheng; his younger brothers are transcribed as Dou and Gen [?]. He married a woman née Mao. He ranked first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second Class: ninety-five men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Cui Xian 崔銑 was registered in Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, in a military household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Zhongfu and ranked sixth in birth order. He was twenty-eight sui and was born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanhe; his grandfather, Gang, was a Treasury Commissioner, granted the honorary title of Secretary and posthumously that of Prefect. His father, Sheng, was Right Administration Vice Commissioner; his mother, née Li, was granted the title Lady of Respect. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xuan and Shi, and his wife was née Li. He placed ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Song 嚴嵩 was registered in Fenyi County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in an artisan household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Weizhong and ranked third in birth order. He was twenty-six sui and was born on the twenty-second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lian; his grandfather, Tingxian; his father, Huai; and his mother, née Yan 晏. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Yue, and his wife was née Ouyang. He placed sixteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhan Ruoshui 湛若水 was registered in Zengcheng County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Yuanming and ranked first in birth order. He was forty sui and was born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather, Jiang; his father, Ying; and his mother, née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zhenxiang, Mengxin, Sheng, Zhongliang, Zhao, Yu, Yucheng, and Zumian; his younger brothers were Ba, Zhen, and Qin [division of the brothers’ names uncertain]. His wife was née Yuan. He placed fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡璉〔貫直隸淮安府沭陽縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字重器，行三，年三十七，十二月初一日生〕。曾祖輔，祖友良，父綱〔遇例冠帶〕，母趙氏。具慶下，兄瑄、玘、珣，娶屠氏。應天府鄉試第一百十三名，會試第五十二名。
translation_en:
Wang Bingliang, courtesy name Bocun, was registered in Xichong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, seventh in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jixian, his grandfather Qing, his father Jun (a National University student), and his mother née He; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Bingyi, Bingneng, and Bingcheng, his younger brothers Binggong and Bingjian, and his wife née He; he ranked twenty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Liu, courtesy name Deqi, was registered in Luzhou, Sichuan, in a military household; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites, ninth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingchun, his grandfather Lin (honored with the cap and sash), his father Yingming, and his mother née Liu; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Huang, Can, Jin, Gui, and Pei, his younger brother Hu, and his wife née Xing; he ranked thirty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ni Zongzheng, courtesy name Benduan, was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yinzhong, his grandfather Shouli, his father Yuanzan, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living; his elder brother was Zongda, his younger brothers Zongzhong, Zongti, and Zongxiang, and his wife née Lü; he ranked thirty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Lian, courtesy name Zhongqi, was registered in Shuyang County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites, third in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Youliang, his father Gang (honored with the cap and sash under applicable regulations), and his mother née Zhao; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Xuan, Qi, and Xun, and his wife née Tu; he ranked 113th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lu Shen 陸深, registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziyuan; he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deheng; his grandfather, Xuan, was a medical official; and his father, Ping, held the honorary title of Official for Longevity. His father's former wife was née Qu, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Han, Lan, Mian, Huai, Zhe, Yue, and Yi; his younger brothers were Rong, Han, Wei, He, Pu, Bo, and Zhou. His wife was née Mei. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Jiao 魏校, registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zicai; he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-three years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Zhong, his father Bi, and his mother née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Xue and his younger brother Xiang. His wife was née Wang. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhai Luan 翟鑾, registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard and a native of Zhucheng County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhongming; he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jisheng, his grandfather Shun, and his father Xuan. His legal mother was née Guo and his birth mother née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Kuang and his younger brother Quan. His wife was née Cai. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ting 王綎, registered in a civilian household in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Suibo; he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Furong, was a vice commissioner of a granary; his grandfather was Gui; his father, Pu, was a county vice magistrate; and his mother was née Niu. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Yue, held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness. His wife was née Wu. He placed 113th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cui Jie, courtesy name Shixing, was registered in an artisan household of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in family order, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxiang; his grandfather, Shiyuan; his father, Zhong, Commissioner of the Office of Imperial Handicrafts under the Ministry of Works; and his mother, née Xu. His parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jun. He married a woman née Peng and subsequently a woman née Ji. He placed forty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Tianhe, courtesy name Jiefu, was registered in a military household in Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in family order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenmu; his grandfather, □□ [annotation: □□, illegible]; his father, Gui, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; and his mother, née Gong, who had been granted the title Lady of Suitability. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tianmin, Tianjue, Tianxi, and Tianxu; his younger brothers were Tianzhi, Tianyou, and Tianxiang. He married a woman née Lu. He placed 107th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xun, courtesy name Yanfu, was registered in a civilian household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in family order, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongrong; his grandfather, Sicheng; his father, Qi, an honorary official for public benefaction; and his mother, née Fang. His parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xiang, and his younger brother was Hong. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Jing, courtesy name Yixian, was registered in a civilian household in Fengxin County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourteenth in family order, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weining; his grandfather, Yu’ang; his father, Dijia; and his mother, née Tu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Shi; his younger brothers were Dan and Zhang. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fortieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

許諫〔貫河南開封府密縣人，國子生，治易經，字□□，行二，□□五月二十七日生〕。曾祖均旺，祖義，父□□，母劉氏，母劉氏。慈侍下，兄士，弟□謨，娶楊氏。河南鄉試第四十九名，會試第一百二十五名。

張鷗〔貫直隸松江府上海縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字九苞，行三，年二十九，六月十五日生〕。曾祖益，祖綸，父燦，母唐氏。嚴侍下，兄鸞、鴍，弟鵷、鶴、鵬、鵠、鶾、鵇，娶吳氏。應天府鄉試第四十四名，會試第一百九十六名。
translation_en:
Xu Jin 徐縉 was registered in a military household of the Rear Guard of the Capital Garrison and was a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zirong, was first in birth order, and was twenty-six years old, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Zhen, had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under the applicable regulations; and his father, Chao, held a seventh-rank prestige title. His father's principal wife was née Ru, and his birth mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Shen, and his wife was née Wang. He placed seventeenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Zhang 郭璋 was registered as a guardsman in the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Dongguang County, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name □qi and was second in birth order; the following two characters are illegible [?]. He was born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Yi, and his father Ru. His father's principal wife was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Li. Both parents were living. Two further characters are illegible [?]. His wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Jian 許諫 was a native of Mi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had an illegible courtesy name (□□) and was second in birth order; the following two characters are illegible [?]. He was born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junwang, his grandfather Yi, and his father's name is illegible (□□). His mother was née Liu; the text repeats “mother née Liu” [?]. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Shi, and his younger brother was □mo. His wife was née Yang. He placed forty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ou 張鷗 was registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Jiubao, was third in birth order, and was twenty-nine years old, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Lun, and his father Can; his mother was née Tang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Luan and Wen (鴍); his younger brothers were Yuan, He, Peng, Hu, Han, and Nian (鵇; reading uncertain [?]). His wife was née Wu. He placed forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qin Wei, courtesy name Shiguan, was registered in a military household in Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather, Hai; his father, Min, a Granary Deputy Commissioner; his mother, née Wang; and his stepmother, née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ren, and his younger brothers were Pei, Lü, Shi, Zhuan, and Xiu. He married a woman née Jia. He ranked sixty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Gu, courtesy name Kongzai, was registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard under an illegible registration category (□□) and was a native of Xiangshan County. A supplementary student at the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Wenbin; his grandfather’s and father’s names are illegible (□□ each); his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. The following four characters are illegible (□□□□). He married a woman née Hong. He ranked sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wenlin, courtesy name Daozheng, was registered in a civilian household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, with two preceding characters illegible (□□). A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the tenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Cuizhong; his grandfather’s name is illegible (□□); his father was Li□; and his mother was née Lu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Wen□, and his younger brothers were Wenfeng, Wen’e, and Wenyuan. He married a woman née Wang. He ranked fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Niu Lu, courtesy name Daoyi, was registered in a civilian household in Baodi County, Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was apparently fourth in birth order (the transcription reads 將四 [?]), aged twenty-six, and born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Fu□; his father, Hong, an honorary official; and his mother, née Lü. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yu, Ming (an honorary official), and Zeng [?]; his younger brothers were Yikui, Yilong, Xiangmian, and Xiangyu. He married a woman née Rui. He ranked fifty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Yin, registered in Jinyun County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jingzhi, and he ranked thirty-fourth among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-seven years old, born on the fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xi, posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Minister of Justice; his grandfather was Cai, an honorary official; his father was Kuang, granted the right to wear official cap and girdle under applicable regulations; and his mother was née Tao. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Bin, Kuan, Jun, Zhou, and Wan. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed fifty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chengren, registered in Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuande, and he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-three years old, born on the fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuanshan, his grandfather was Gongyi, his father was Lin, an honorary official, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Chengwen. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed fifty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Yifang, registered in an official household at Jingzhou Guard, Chen Prefecture, Huguang, was originally from Yingtian Prefecture and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yiqing, and he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty years old, born on the seventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Wenchang, his grandfather was □ [name illegible], his father was Di, and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yizhong and Yizheng. He married a woman née Feng. He placed sixty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Tingji, registered in Huarong County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Bingji, and he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-five years old, born on the third day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Qiong, his grandfather was Jun, his father was Keyi, a Prefectural School Professor, and his mother was née Lu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Tingxiang, a Department Magistrate. He married a woman née Chen. He placed fifty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
An Jin 安金, courtesy name Ruli, was registered in a military household in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Yangqu County, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ci; his grandfather, Gui; and his father, Jing, a Gentleman for Rendering Service. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother née Shi. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Yu was a Gentleman for Rendering Service. He married a woman née Xi and subsequently women née Lu and Xiang. He placed seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Jing 沈璟, courtesy name Mengguang, was registered in a civilian household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-one years old, born on the twenty-second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather’s and father’s names are illegible (□□ and □□). His mother was née He. Both parents were living. An elder brother, □, and younger brothers, □ and □□, are listed, their names illegible. He married a woman née Jing. He placed eighty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Jue 江珏, courtesy name Chaozhong, was registered in a medical household in Jinxi County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the first day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Baizhou; his grandfather’s and father’s names are illegible (□□ and □□). His mother was née Peng. His father was deceased and his mother living. An elder brother, □, and younger brothers, □ and □□, are listed, their names illegible. He married a woman née Huang. He placed eighty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Chan 沈燀, courtesy name Jingming, was registered in a civilian household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked thirteenth among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xun 桪; his grandfather’s name is transcribed as “Pf” [?]; his father was Bing 昞; and his mother was née Yue. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Mao 暓, and his younger brother Shi 時. He married a woman née Jin. He placed eighty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ning He was registered in a military household of Dingbian Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Jishan County, Shanxi. A student of the government school of Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Bodong; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shisi; his grandfather, Gang, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father, Xian, was a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhu. His mother alone survived. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jinxian was registered in a military household of Dengzhou, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was □bin; he ranked first in birth order and was forty years old, born on the twenty-first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuan; his grandfather, Pan; his father, Sheng; his mother, née Zhou; and his stepmother, née Xia. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jin□, and his younger brother was □□. He married a woman née Zhao as his subsequent wife. He placed sixteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xian was registered in a commoner household of Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was □□; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-one years old, born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Zong; his father, □; his mother, née Zheng; and his birth mother, née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brother was □, and his younger brother was □. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chai Yi was registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the military school of the capital guards, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Shizhong; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Xiuchun, and grandfather, Qing, were each posthumously appointed Company Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; his father, Run, was a Company Commander in that guard. His mother, née Huang, was invested with the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ren, and his younger brother, Li, held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness. He married a woman née Sun. He placed eighty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Xiu 孫脩, courtesy name Yongji, was registered in the military ranks of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Handan County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in birth order and was twenty-eight sui, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shi’an; his grandfather Gui was posthumously appointed Vice Commander; and his father Xian was Vice Commander. His father’s former principal wife was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Sun. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Jun, a Vice Commander, Jie, and Ru, a Squad Commander. He married a woman née Gu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Yun 陸芸, courtesy name Shiqian, belonged to the military register of the Jinchi military office in Yunnan and was a native of Wu County in the directly administered region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked sixth in birth order and was thirty-one sui, born on the eighteenth day of the intercalary sixth month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Zhen, his father Pu, and his mother née Kang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhi, Mao, Hui, and Rao; his younger brothers were Hua and E. He married a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-fifth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and one hundred tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jiuxu 張九敘, courtesy name Yugong, belonged to the military register of Shanghe County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth in birth order and was thirty-two sui, born on the fifth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zongyan; his grandfather Zheng was honorifically appointed Investigating Censor and posthumously appointed Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his father Da was Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His father’s former wife, née Liu, was posthumously granted the title Lady for Service (ruren); his mother, née Zhao, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Suizuo, Jiusi, Jiuchou, and Jiuze; his younger brothers were Jiushao, Jiugao, and Jiude. He married a woman née Liu. He placed seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ce 陳策, courtesy name Wanyan, belonged to the civilian register of Shan County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-four sui, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather Xun was posthumously appointed Vice Commissioner of the Left in the Office of Transmission; and his father Xu held that office. His mother, née Shan, was granted the title Lady of Suitability (yiren). Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhao and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yao Jiyan 姚繼巖, courtesy name Yuanxiao, was from Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in Zhili, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the subprefectural government school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second in family order and was aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingfan; his grandfather, Jing; and his father, Xuan, a School Instructor. His father's former wife was Lady Hu, and his mother was Lady Zhao. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Jichong, and his younger brothers were Song, Yue, Yi, and Long. He married Lady Huang. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhan Yuan 詹源, courtesy name Shiyuan, was from Anxi County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in family order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qianqing; his grandfather, Jing, a District Magistrate; his father, Jin; and his mother, Lady Lin. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zhen and Han. He married Lady Wu. He placed fifteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jie 劉節, courtesy name Jiefu, was from Dayu County, Nan'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenyuan; his grandfather's and father's names are illegible (□ and □); and his mother was Lady Ou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Ji, and his younger brother was Ce. He married Lady Zhou. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Dan 潘旦, courtesy name Xizhou, was from Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in Zhili, and registered in a military household. A student of the prefectural government school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zesheng; his grandfather, Guilian; his father, Chuanxian; and his mother, Lady Dai. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhao, Fang, and Jian. He married Lady Cheng. He placed twenty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Lianghan, courtesy name Zhongshen, was registered in an artisan household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Di; his grandfather, Xuan, held the honorary title of Official for Righteous Service; his father was Qian, and his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Liangfu, and his wife was née Lü. He placed twenty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xi, courtesy name Youqing, was registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twenty-second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fa; his grandfather, Zhong, was a National University student; his father was Hong, and his mother was née Lin. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Tie, Fu, and “Rv” [?], and his wife was née Wu. He placed seventy-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jin, courtesy name Wenshi, was registered in a civilian household in Sui Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. An Assistant Instructor specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather was Lin, his father was Neng, and his mother was née Sun. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Jian, and his wife was née Liu. He placed eightieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Hu, courtesy name Ruiqing, was registered in a military household in Chao County, Wuwei Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Heng, was a District Magistrate; and his father, Guang, was an Instructor. His father's former wife was née Chen, his mother was née Gao, and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother Huan was a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his wife was née Zhang. He placed 103rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liao Ji, courtesy name Weixiu, was registered in an officer household of Jiujiang Guard in Zhili and was a native of Huangmei County, Huguang. A student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ronggui; his grandfather, Xian; his father, Zhen, a Company Commander; and his mother, née Pan. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Gang, was a Company Commander; his younger brothers were Lun, Xiu, Ji, Shou, and Wei. His wife was née Feng. He placed seventy-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Yuan, courtesy name Jingzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the twelfth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kexin; his grandfather, Zhang; his father, Wen□ [?]; and his mother, née He. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Ji, Yan, Jin, Can, □ [name illegible], Qia, Hong, and Qian. His wife was née Zeng. He placed sixty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Chao, courtesy name Juyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the National University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mingshan; his grandfather, Tinggui; his father, Dasheng, an honorary official; and his mother, née Du. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hai, Yan, Hao, and Yang; his younger brothers were Hao, Ji, and Xie. His first wife was née Chen, and his subsequent wife was née Hong. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Xue, courtesy name Risheng, was registered in a military household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mindao; his grandfather, Jian; his father, Dang; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiang, Xu, and Shu; his younger brother was Jiong. His wife was née Zou. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張繼孟〔貫錦衣衛籍，浙江仁和縣人，順天府學生，治書經，字子醇，行一，年二十九，六月二十六日生〕。曾祖彥和，祖全，父泰，母劉氏。具慶下，娶郎氏。順天府鄉試第四十三名，會試第十六名。

周墨〔貫直隸蘇州府太倉州民籍，國子生，治詩經，字文卿，行二，年三十七，九月十四日生〕。曾祖公舟〔聽選官〕，祖記，父鵷，母徐氏，繼母凌氏。具慶下，兄坤〔貢士〕，弟璧、塾、垔，娶奚氏。應天府鄉試第七十七名，會試第二百二十六名。

劉鵬〔貫武驤右衛軍籍，山西太原府石州人，國子生，治詩經，字大舉，行一，年二十八，七月十一日生〕。曾祖福源，祖聚，父寧，母王氏。具慶下，娶王氏，繼娶羅氏。順天府鄉試第四十名，會試第一百三十七名。

向文璽〔貫湖廣荊州府夷陵州宜都縣民籍，州學生，治易經，字國信，行六，年二十六，八月初五日生〕。曾祖中庸，祖庭蕙，父冕，前母吳氏，母吳氏。具慶下，兄文琳、文琇、文珪、文瑞，弟文璧、文琮，娶陳氏。湖廣鄉試第二十三名，會試第二百五名。
translation_en:
Zhang Jimeng, courtesy name Zichun, was registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang. A student of the Shuntian Prefectural School, he specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked first among his brothers, and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanhe; his grandfather, Quan; his father, Tai; and his mother, née Liu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Lang. He placed forty-third in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Mo, courtesy name Wenqing, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked second among his brothers, and was thirty-seven years old, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongzhou, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his grandfather, Ji; his father, Yuan; his mother, née Xu; and his stepmother, née Ling. Both parents were living. His elder brother Kun was a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Bi, Shu, and Yin. His wife was née Xi. He placed seventy-seventh in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Peng, courtesy name Daju, was registered in a military household of the Wuxiang Right Guard and was a native of Shi Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first among his brothers, and was twenty-eight years old, born on the eleventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuyuan; his grandfather, Ju; his father, Ning; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Wang; his subsequent wife was née Luo. He placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Wenxi, courtesy name Guoxin, was registered in a civilian household in Yidu County, Yiling Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked sixth among his brothers, and was twenty-six years old, born on the fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongyong; his grandfather, Tinghui; and his father, Mian. His father's former wife and his mother were both née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wenlin, Wenxiu, Wengui, and Wenrui; his younger brothers were Wenbi and Wencong. His wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

盛儀〔貫直隸揚州衛軍籍，江都縣人，國子生，治易經，字德章，行三，年二十九，正月二十二日生〕。曾祖彬，祖安，父弘，母董氏。具慶下，兄儒、健，弟俊、傑、佐、佑，娶姜氏。應天府鄉試第六名，會試第二百十二名。

李志剛〔貫四川成都右護衛軍籍，山西崞縣人，國子生，治詩經，字近仁，行二，年二十八，三月初八日生〕。曾祖仁信，祖亮，父明，母張氏。永感下，弟志端，娶党氏。四川鄉試第五十八名，會試第二百五十七名。

顧可學〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字與成，行一，年二十四，四月初二日生〕。曾祖壽，祖信，父榮〔義官〕，母馬氏。具慶下，弟可適、可立、可久、可大、可遠、可賢、可宗，娶馬氏。應天府鄉試第九十九名，會試第一百三十九名。

閔槐〔貫直隸河間府任丘縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字公甫，行一，年二十九，九月初五日生〕。曾祖彝〔貢士〕，祖琦，父定〔聽選官〕，母卞氏。具慶下，弟楷〔同科進士〕，娶顏氏。順天府鄉試第十四名，會試第四十一名。
translation_en:
Sheng Yi, courtesy name Dezhang, was registered in a military household of Yangzhou Guard in Zhili and was a native of Jiangdu County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather An, and his father Hong; his mother was née Dong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ru and Jian, and his younger brothers Jun, Jie, Zuo, and You. His wife was née Jiang. He placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhigang, courtesy name Jinren, was registered in a military household of the Chengdu Right Escort Guard in Sichuan and was a native of Guo County, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Renxin, his grandfather Liang, and his father Ming; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Zhiduan, and his wife was née Dang. He placed fifty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Kexue, courtesy name Yucheng, was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shou, his grandfather Xin, and his father Rong, an honorary official; his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Keshi, Keli, Kejiu, Keda, Keyuan, Kexian, and Kezong. His wife was née Ma. He placed ninety-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Min Huai, courtesy name Gongfu, was registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his grandfather was Qi, and his father Ding, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His mother was née Bian. Both parents were living. His younger brother Kai was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year, and his wife was née Yan. He placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

方位〔貫江西廣信府弋陽縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字惟立，行七十六，年二十九，九月十七日生〕。曾祖伯廣，祖思本，父重〔義官〕，母張氏。永感下，兄定、廣、積、健、伯安，娶蘇氏，繼娶李氏。江西鄉試第二十二名，會試第一百七十二名。

李緋〔貫河南汝寧府光州固始縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字廷章，行三，年三十四，六月十六日生〕。曾祖子貴，祖瑄，父灦〔訓導〕，母陳氏。具慶下，兄碏、翠，弟綠、紺，娶張氏。河南鄉試第六名，會試第二百七名。

徐子熙〔貫浙江紹興府上虞縣，軍籍，縣學生，治禮記，字世昭，行一，年五十，十月初三日生〕。曾祖彥誠，祖清，父杰〔主簿〕，母王氏，繼母齊氏。慈侍下，弟子然、子魚、子謙、子竒，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第三名，會試第一百一名。
translation_en:
Sun Tai, registered in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shiyin, he ranked third in his family, and he was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongchang, his grandfather Yuanrui, his father Bin, and his mother née Fei; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yu and Fu, his younger brothers Yi and Cui, and his wife was née Yang. He placed seventy-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Wei, registered in Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Weili, he ranked seventy-sixth in his family, and he was twenty-nine years old, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boguang, his grandfather Siben, his father Zhong, an honorary official, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ding, Guang, Ji, Jian, and Bo'an [name division uncertain: possibly Bo and An]; his first wife was née Su, and he subsequently married a woman née Li. He placed twenty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Fei, registered in Gushi County, Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingzhang, he ranked third in his family, and he was thirty-four years old, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zigui, his grandfather Xuan, his father Xian, an Assistant Instructor, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Que and Cui, his younger brothers Lü and Gan, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zixi, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shizhao, he ranked first in his family, and he was fifty years old, born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yancheng, his grandfather Qing, his father Jie, a Registrar, his mother née Wang, and his stepmother née Qi; his father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Ziran, Ziyu, Ziqian, and Ziqi, and his wife was née Chen. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Shou, courtesy name Chaoyong, was registered with the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Yanshan County, Cangzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongyan, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Jian; his father's former wife was née Hu, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shen, and his wife was née Ma. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Youduan, courtesy name De□ [?], had civilian registration in Baishui County, Tongzhou, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a native of Qianyang County, Fengxiang Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he was sixth in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the tenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liangfu; his grandfather's name is illegible (□□), as is the annotation following it (□□□); his father was Shi, with an illegible annotation (□□□□). His mother, née Liu, was granted the title Lady of Gentleness. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Bin, Chun, Youcai, Youzhong, and Youliang; his younger brothers were Youying, Yourang, Youzhi, and Youfang. His wife was née Yuan. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Qing, courtesy name Ruzhong, had civilian registration in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. A prefectural school student, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Zhiyuan, his father Qi, and his mother née Xiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Fu, whose entry has an illegible annotation (□□□□), and Lin; his younger brother was Yong. His wife was née Dai. He ranked thirty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Wenzuan, courtesy name Dexu, had civilian registration in Huai'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he was ninth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the tenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xinren; his grandfather Xiu was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his father Yu was a tribute scholar (gongshi); and his mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady of Repose. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Wenlu, and his wife was née Wu. He ranked eighty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Wendi, registered in Ningde County, Funing Subprefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tingji, he was fifth in birth order, and he was forty years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Guan, an Assistant Instructor posthumously appointed Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather was Jicheng; his father was Zhu, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Zheng. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Wentong and Wenqian, and his wife was née Huang. He ranked first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Boxiang, registered in Tongliang County, He Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Bingjun, he was first in birth order, and he was forty years old, born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wenhuan; his grandfather was Huai; his father was Youqing; and his mother was née Zhu. His father alone was still living. His younger brother was Boyu, and his wife was née Yu. He ranked sixty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Huang, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Mingshao, he was first in birth order, and he was thirty years old, born on the second day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ziyun; his grandfather was Qianning; his father was Yitai; and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were still living. His younger brother was Sheng, and his wife was née Yao. He ranked fifty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Ming, registered in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Kexin, he was first in birth order, and he was forty years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Guansheng; his grandfather was Chongwen; his father was Qi; his mother was née Tan; and his stepmother was née Mai. Both parents were still living. His younger brothers were Jian, Wu, Jin, and Xian, and his wife was née Li. He ranked fifty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Donggao, registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Rudeng, he ranked fourth in family birth order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Li, his father Hui, and his mother née Chai; his parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Dongshan, Dongming, and Dongyang, and his younger brothers Dongyuan, Dongpu, Dongyuan, Dongjin, Donglan, and Donghu; he married a woman née Sun. He placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Pang, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Boyu, he ranked forty-second in family birth order, and he was aged twenty-five, born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xie, his grandfather Tan, his father Lian, and his mother née Wang; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hai, Zhang, Cheng, Wen, Chun, and Hong; he married a woman née Qian. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yuan, registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shida, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Yingzhen, his father Shiliang, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living. His elder brother was Fu and his younger brother Dong; he married a woman née Zhuang. He placed seventy-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Guan, registered in a civilian household in Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dacheng, he ranked thirty-first in family birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunjian, his grandfather Anyi, his father Qin, and his mother née Xiao; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Huai, a School Instructor, and Han, and his younger brother was Si; he married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed seventy-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

諸絢，貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣匠籍，國子生。治禮記，字用晦，行十五，年三十六，二月初八日生。曾祖勝宗，祖□，父諫〔教諭〕，母周氏，繼母毛氏。具慶下，兄縑〔監生〕、縝、統、績、絃、綬、紋、縉、榮、絢、絡、經、縯、維，娶張氏。浙江鄉試第二十二名，會試第二百六十七名。

熊遇，貫河南儀衛司校籍，江西豐城縣人，汝寧府學生。治詩經，字道夫，行一，年二十八，五月初四日生。曾祖貴，祖正，父□〔□〕，母劉氏。具慶下，弟遵、逵、選，娶白氏。河南鄉試第三名，會試第五十七名。

向一陽，貫四川成都府雙流縣民籍，湖廣巴陵縣人，國子生。治易經，字汝葵，行二，年三十六，十二月二十三日生。曾祖文貴，祖洪，父明，嫡母黃氏，生母方氏。慈侍下，兄南陽，弟丹陽、輝陽、得陽，娶高氏，繼娶姜氏。四川鄉試第五十八名，會試第七十四名。
translation_en:
Cai Xu was registered in an officer household of the Jinwu Right Guard and was a native of Baodi County, Shuntian Prefecture; he was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Shiyong, and ranked third among his brothers; he was twenty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Gui and grandfather Xiang were both Assistant Regional Military Commissioners; his father Ying was an Assistant Regional Military Commissioner serving as Left Assistant Regional Commander. His father's former wife, née Zhao, had been granted the title Lady of Gentleness; his mother was née Shang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Lin, currently serving as Guard Commander, and Wen; his younger brothers were Ting, Lu, Zhan, and Yin. He married a woman née Wei. He placed seventy-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Xuan was registered in an artisan household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites, had the courtesy name Yonghui, and ranked fifteenth among his brothers; he was thirty-six, born on the eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shengzong, his grandfather's name is illegible, and his father Jian was a County School Instructor; his mother was née Zhou, and his stepmother was née Mao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jian, an Imperial University student, Zhen, Tong, Ji, Xian, Shou, Wen, Jin, Rong, Xuan [?; the same character as his own given name], Luo, Jing, Yan, and Wei. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Yu was registered as a guardsman in the Henan Ceremonial Guard Office and was a native of Fengcheng County, Jiangxi; he was a student of the Runing Prefectural School. He specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Daofu, and ranked first among his brothers; he was twenty-eight, born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui and his grandfather was Zheng; his father's name and the accompanying annotation are illegible. His mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zun, Kui, and Xuan. He married a woman née Bai. He placed third in the Henan Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Yiyang was registered in a civilian household in Shuangliu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, and was a native of Baling County, Huguang; he was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Rukui, and ranked second among his brothers; he was thirty-six, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wengui, his grandfather was Hong, and his father was Ming; his legal mother was née Huang, and his birth mother was née Fang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Nanyang; his younger brothers were Danyang, Huiyang, and Deyang. He married a woman née Gao and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He placed fifty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Zhong, registered in Luzhou, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xianzhi; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenliang; his grandfather, Zhi; and his father, Tingzan, a School Instructor. His legal mother and birth mother were both née Liu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Ai, Xian, Qing, Hui, and En; his younger brothers were Ning, Yi, and Yu. His wife was née Wei. He placed forty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

An Bang, registered in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yanchen; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the fourteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Changtai; his grandfather, Zhi; and his father, Bengao. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Zhuang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ren, Li, Xiang, and Jun; his younger brothers were Biao, Tan, Fen, Chun, and He. His wife was née Su. He placed seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Hong’en, registered in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zicheng; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged twenty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Biwen; his grandfather, Kai; and his father, Dechun, a tribute student. His mother was née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hongxian; his younger brothers were Hongzhun, Hongfan, and Hongde. His wife was née Jiang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shu Biao, registered in Tongliang County, Hezhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Minwang; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhigao; his grandfather, Quan; and his father, Daoxing. His mother was née Gao. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Jian. His wife was née Yang. He placed forty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Han, courtesy name Houfu, was registered in a civilian household in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was an additional student of the county Confucian school and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and born on the twenty-third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Chen; his father’s former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yan 嵒 and Que; his younger brothers were Yan 嵓, Mi, and Shan. His wife was née Sun. He placed sixty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhan Kui, courtesy name Wenhui, was registered in a military household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan; he was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Rites. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Bichang, his father Chonglu, and his mother née Yang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Bi, Li, Zhi, Shi, and Hou. His wife was née Liu. He placed seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Chentu, courtesy name Longfu, was registered in an artisan household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Wucheng County; he was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Classic of Changes. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingchang, his grandfather Jian, and his father Shou; his father’s principal wife was née Lu, and his mother was née Yin. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Daguan and Dalin. His wife was née Ge. He placed ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Bin, courtesy name Jiezhi, was registered in a civilian household in Dezhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong; he was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-four and born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Fu, his father Tong〔a tribute scholar, gongshi〕, and his mother née Zhong. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Xiang and Jian. His wife was née Chen. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Qi, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in an official household of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was originally from Chengcheng County, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Zhi; his father, Zhen (a Dahan General [?] and company commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard); and his mother, née Lu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Lin, and his wife was née Jiang. He placed seventy-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Ji, courtesy name Ruji, was registered in a civilian household in Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was originally from Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zi□; his grandfather, Yanlian (a district magistrate); his father, Shirong; and his mother, née Xie. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Tai, followed by three illegible characters (□□□) [?]; his wife was née Chen. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zan, courtesy name Tingxian, was registered in an artisan household of the Left Guard of Generals and was originally from Cangzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ju; his grandfather’s name is illegible (□□); his father was Rong; his mother was née Wang; and his stepmother was née Cui. Both parents were living. His wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was née Yang. He placed eightieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Ne, courtesy name Shangmin, was registered in a military household in Leiyang County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the fourteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Yongchang; his grandfather, Bixian (a department magistrate); his father, Wenxiang (Huicheng [?], formerly an investigating censor); and his mother, née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zi (an assistant prefect) and Yi (a tribute scholar); his younger brothers were E, Hui, Yan, and Fang. His wife was née Zhang. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Dingzhi, registered in a civilian household in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhunqing; he ranked second in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wushao, his grandfather Gong, his father Kui, and his mother née Tang. Both parents were living. His elder brother Xingzhi had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations. He married a woman née Lin. He placed twenty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zhenqing, registered in a military household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Changgu; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the tenth day of the intercalary tenth month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Xian, and his father Yu, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations. His father's former wife was née Zhang, his mother née Tang, and his stepmother née Shi. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xiangqing. He married a woman née Gao. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jian, registered in a military household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was originally from Lin'an County, Zhejiang. He was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yunjing; he ranked third in his family and was forty years old, born on the twentieth day of an illegible month. His great-grandfather was Pingtian, his grandfather Dayong, his father Zhong, and his mother née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brother's name is illegible (□□). He married a woman née Tang. His rank in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination was 1□□; he placed thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Tang, registered in a civilian household in Jinxian County, an illegible prefecture (□□) in Jiangxi, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shiming; he ranked eighteenth in his family and was twenty-one years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Dequan and his grandfather Yuanhe, whose annotation reads “Prefectural School Instructor, under applicable regulations” [?]. His father Fu was a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, and his mother, née Rao, had been granted the title Lady of Suitability. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Shisheng, Shilu, Zi, Qi, Qin, Rui, Jiao, and Sui; his younger brother was Gao. He married a woman née Yang. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.
