translation_en:
Third Class: 205 men, granted the status of equivalent metropolitan graduates (jinshi).

Duan Jiong 段炅 was registered in a military household in Lanzhou, Lintao Prefecture, Shaanxi, with ancestral origins in Yangqu County, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Jingming and ranked third in his family. He was thirty-two years old, born on the fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Minghe was a Magistrate; his grandfather was Wen□, and his father’s name is illegible. His mother, née Yao [?], held the conferred title of Lady; his birth mother was née Yang. His father was deceased and his mother surviving. He had an elder brother whose name is illegible and younger brothers Ang, □, and Hao. His wife was née Shi. He placed twenty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Liangzuo 王良佐 was registered in a civilian household in Yiling Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Liangbi and ranked second in his family. He was thirty-two years old, born on the tenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Wenxuan was posthumously granted the title Gentleman for Meritorious Service [four following characters illegible]; his grandfather’s name is illegible, and his father Kui was a Supervising Secretary. His mother, née Liu, held the conferred title of Lady. Both his parents were living. His elder brothers were Liangchen, Liangfu, Liang□, Liangyong, Liangqi, and Liangjin. His wife was née Wu; he subsequently married a woman née Du. He placed thirty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Lan 田瀾 was registered in a civilian household in Chang’an County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Ruguan and ranked third in his family. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingchun; his grandfather Mao was an Assistant Prefect, and his father Geng was an Instructor. His father’s former wives were née Ma and née Wang; his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother surviving. His elder brothers were Pu and Guan, and his younger brother was Can. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Mingbi 周明弼, courtesy name Mengliang, was from Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and belonged to a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongqian; his grandfather, Zonghe; and his father, Xiang, a Chief Clerk. His father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Huang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Xiang 瓖, and his younger brothers were Mingyou and Mingjun. His wife was née Zhao. He placed sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Tianyou 蔡天祐, courtesy name Chengzhi, was from Sui Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and belonged to a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty, born on the first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Jing, held the prestige title Grand Master for Governance; and his father, Sheng, was a Prefect. His legal mother was née Hu, invested with the title Lady of Suitability, and his birth mother was née Liu. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Tianzuo and Tianlu, and his wife was née Han. He placed forty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zhi 黃質, courtesy name Wenzhi, was from Fan County, Pu Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, and belonged to a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-one, born on the seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuzhao, a County Magistrate; his grandfather, Xun; and his father, Huan 瓛. His father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Guan, his younger brother was Shi, and his wife was née Song. He placed forty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Chengliang 劉澄亮, courtesy name Shengming, was from Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and belonged to an artisan household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in birth order and was aged forty-eight, born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongjing; his grandfather, Minjie; and his father, Ding, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His mother was née Hu. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Chengcan, Chengji, Chenglian, and Chenghui, and his wife was née Fu. He placed sixtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiang Wenmin, registered in a civilian household in Jingde County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Kexue; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was twenty-five sui, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yixing; his grandfather, Shangzhi, was posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father, Han, was a Prefect. His father's former wife, née Rui, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren); his mother, née Liu, was granted the same title. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Jifu and Wenqin, and his younger brother was Chang. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed 118th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ou Yue, registered in a military household in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a Directorate of Education student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenguang; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight sui, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziquan; his grandfather, Minrui; and his father, Jian. His mother was née Song, and his stepmother was née Tang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chao, Qi, Qi (𧺫) [?], and Fu. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yan, registered in a military household in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, was a Directorate of Education student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Minwang; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-nine sui, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuxing; his grandfather, Gui; and his father, Cheng, a Department Magistrate. His mother was née Xue, and his stepmother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ru; his younger brothers were Wei, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Yu. He married a woman née Du. He placed 109th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Chi, registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a Directorate of Education student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Dejie; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-eight sui, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhou, was granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather, Shugang, was a Reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy; and his father was Wei. His mother was née Ye. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Xi, Li [?], Zhang, and Da, the last of whom also became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in this examination year. He married a woman née Huang. He placed nineteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zheng Xing, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Huai'an County School. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shiji; he ranked sixth among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shu, an honorary longevity official; his grandfather was Wenshao, and his father was Mingqian. His mothers are listed as Lady Zhang and Lady Chen [?], and his stepmother as Lady Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shizuo, a Vice Prefect, Shijian, Shixu, and Shiruo; his younger brother was Shize. He married Lady Chen and subsequently married another Lady Chen. He placed twelfth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Duo, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shizhen; he ranked twenty-second among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-five years old, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongkui, his grandfather Zongjie, his father Binghe, and his mother Lady Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jin, Yin, and Zhen; his younger brothers were Jian, Xin, and Jun. He married Lady Zhou. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Pu, registered in Longquan County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shiyong; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-five years old, born on the nineteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chongmao, his grandfather Yichang, his father Zhifan, and his mother Lady Chen. Both parents were living. He married Lady Shen and subsequently married Lady Guan. He placed fifty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Heng, registered in Jishui County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yizhen; he ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins and was forty-three years old, born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizhan, a Registrar; his grandfather was Yongding, and his father was Ning, an Instructor. His legal mothers were Lady Luo and Lady Xie; his birth mother was Lady He. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jueyi and Juezhong; his younger brother was Juehou. He married Lady Song. He placed thirty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tang 王鏜 was registered in an official household of the Yingzhou Central Garrison Guard under the Daning Regional Military Commission and was a native of Xuzhou in Zhili. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Yansheng, ranked fifth among his brothers, and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather Xuan, his father Lin, and his mother née Li; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiong (a Company Commander), Rui, Jian, and Ying. His wife was née Xu. He placed seventy-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Kui 陳逵 was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An added student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had an illegible courtesy-name passage [?] and was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhou (honorarily granted the title of Investigating Censor); his grandfather’s and father’s names are illegible [?], as is the annotation following his father’s name [?]. His mother was née Ye, and both parents were living. His elder brother’s name and the names of two younger brothers are illegible [?]; another younger brother was Xian. His wife was née Wang. His placing in the Fujian Provincial Examination is illegible [?]; he placed 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zhu 黃著 was registered in a military household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he had an illegible courtesy-name passage [?] and was twenty-eight years old, born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youguang; his grandfather’s and father’s names are illegible [?]. His mother was née Yin and his stepmother née Feng; the entry records both parents as living. His elder brother’s name and one younger brother’s name are illegible [?]; his other younger brothers were Xuan and Dan. His wife was née Tan. He placed ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yuan 胡遠 was registered in a civilian household in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Ziming, ranked eighteenth among his brothers, and was thirty-nine years old, born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zihao, his grandfather Fangji, his father Xiangxun, and his mother née Liao; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuanhui, Yuanjun, and Yuanmian. His wife was née Yuan. He placed fifty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Yaofeng, courtesy name Boqi, was registered in a civilian household in Dingxing County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Dexin, his father Liang, and his mother née Wei. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yaoqing and his younger brother Yaozi; his wife was née Song. He ranked seventy-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Luan, courtesy name Mingzhong, was registered in a salt-producing household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the tenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Zizheng, his grandfather Fu, and his father Maoqian; the text lists a mother née Yu and another mother née Ma [?]. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Mou; his wife was née Zhu. He ranked ninetieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yi Mo, courtesy name Jiayan, was registered in a civilian household in Gushi County, Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. An additional-quota county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wei, an administrative assistant; his grandfather was Ben, his father Lin, an Imperial University student, and his mother née Deng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yi, Fang, Xun, Xun, Jin, Yong, Cheng, and Gao; his wife was née Yu. He ranked fifty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Lan, courtesy name Ziqing, was registered in a military household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was sixth in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Guiliang, his grandfather Gongzheng, who was granted the title of vice director, his father was recorded as “ab” [?], and his mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Meng, an administration vice commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, Jin, and Zhan; his younger brothers were Ziming, a tribute scholar, and Zili, an investigating censor. His wife was née Li. He ranked ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Guan, registered in Daozhou, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the department school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yixian. He ranked second in family order, was twenty-three, and was born on the fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shou (holder of an honorary longevity title); his grandfather was Shaotong; his father was Wenyuan; and his mother was née He. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Tang. He was betrothed to a woman née Liao. He placed sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Hong, registered in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the county school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Jingzhan. He ranked thirty-second in family order, was twenty-eight, and was born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Bowen (posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Rites); his grandfather was Gui; his father was Zhao; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Bang, Tao, and Yan, and his younger brother was Chuo. His wife was née Xie. He placed forty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Lun, registered in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student at the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Chaozhang. He ranked first in family order, was thirty-eight, and was born on the first day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Mengli; his grandfather was Cheng; his father was Heng; his mother was née Ge; and his stepmothers were née Ding and née Yao. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Tang. He placed fifty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yichu, registered in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Chaoshuo. He ranked first in family order, was thirty, and was born on the first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Kezhang; his grandfather was Yisi; his father was Shi’an; and his mother was née Huang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Zhao, Ting, Cong, Mo, Bi, Rui, Ding, Zhen, and Han. He married a woman née Chen. He placed fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Hua 吳華, courtesy name Dehui, was registered in a military household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wu, his grandfather Zhao, his father Fu, and his mother née Huang; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lan and Ying. He married a woman née Jie and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed sixteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shu’an 張叔安, courtesy name Yueqing, was registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yanli was a yin-yang official, posthumously conferred the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather Jie was a Prefect; his father was Zuobiao, and his mother was née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Shuding; his younger brothers were Shukuan, Shuxuan, Shuguan, Shushou, Shuzong, Shushen, Shubao, Shucai, Shujun, Shuyi, Shuhui, and Shuhe. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fifteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jue 李玨, courtesy name Tingzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the tenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuan, his grandfather Jing, and his father Cheng; his father's former wife was née Wu, his mother was née Sun, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Qin. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Fang 王坊, courtesy name Chongxian, was registered in an artisan household in Huangyan County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongmin; his grandfather Ju was an Assistant Judge of a subprefecture, conferred the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father Bi was a Prefect; and his mother, née Ding, was conferred the title of Lady of Tranquility. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Pei and Zeng; his younger brothers were Chi, Lei, Dong, and Tai. He married a woman née Sun. He placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ma Sicong, courtesy name Maowen, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guisun, his grandfather Wei, and his father Chun’er; his mother was née Fang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Siwen and Sizhong, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed sixty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Gongshao, courtesy name Dahe, was registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked eleventh among his brothers and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather Yougong was a county magistrate, and his father Qinan was an assistant prefect. His father’s former wife and his mother were both née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Gongting, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); Gongtang, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Gongmian; Gongyun; Gongyu, a commissioner; and Gongjia, a county magistrate. His younger brothers were Gongxia, Gonghu, Gongwu, and Gongshao (公勺). His wife was née Ran. He placed sixty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Yu, courtesy name Chaoyi, was registered in an artisan household in Guiyang Subprefecture, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yitong; his grandfather Liang was an unranked assistant official; his father was Xi, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qi and Lin, his younger brothers were Yan and Jie, and his wife was née Xiao. He placed forty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Tingqiong, courtesy name Ke’ai, was registered in a military household of Xiangyang Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Huai’an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Xiangyang prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged twenty-two, born on the seventeenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Qian, and his father Ji, a vice prefect. His legal mother was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Wang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Tingbi, Tingzan, and Tinglian, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed forty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

王一麟〔貫四川眉州青神縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字明瑞，行六，年三十三，十月初七日生〕。曾祖真，祖必高，父坤，前母孫氏，母謝氏。具慶下，兄伯昌、伯清、伯灝、伯萬、伯政，弟伯海、伯溟，娶楊氏。四川鄉試第三十七名，會試第五十一名。
translation_en:
Ou Xing 區行, registered in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhongxing, he ranked sixth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Mingshan, and his father Jin; his father's principal wife was née Huang, and his birth mother was née Lu. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Liang, Wenyu, Wenjun, Wenhui, and Wenyuan, and his wife was née Luo. He placed twenty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xian Mian 鮮冕, registered in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Wenqing, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zong, his grandfather Yonghua, and his father Jun, a prefectural vice prefect; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Ao and Gun, his younger brother was Hu, and his wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yuan 黃瑗, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Chunyu, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongzhang, his grandfather Daguang, and his father Sheng; his mother was née Jiang, and his stepmother was née Wu. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Kuan, a tribute student (gongshi), his younger brothers were Ne, Que, and Lie, and his wife was née Su. He placed fifty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yilin 王一麟, registered in Qingshen County, Meizhou, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Mingrui, he ranked sixth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Bigao, and his father Kun; his father's former wife was née Sun, and his mother was née Xie. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Bochang, Boqing, Bohao, Bowan, and Bozheng, his younger brothers were Bohai and Boming, and his wife was née Yang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳昂〔貫浙江嘉興府海鹽縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字德翼，行二，年三十六，正月初七日生〕。曾祖繼，祖顯〔遇例冠帶〕，父寬，前母馬氏，母鄭氏。重慶下，兄昇，弟冕、昱、昺，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第十四名，會試第一百三十二名。

孫樂〔貫山東登州府福山縣軍籍，縣學生，治禮記，字燮卿，行五，年三十二，七月十五日生〕。曾祖彥斌〔贈知府〕，祖遇〔左布政使，贈正奉大夫、正治卿〕，父琰〔尚寶司少卿〕，母李氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄棨〔監生〕、槩、棐〔同科進士〕，pol弟楶、棠、果、棅、桇、栗、桌，娶李氏，繼娶謝氏。山東鄉試第七十二名，會試第八十三名。

林潮〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣民籍，府學生，治易經，字君信，行一，年三十六，七月初四日生〕。曾祖克玉，祖資允，父凱，母楊氏，繼母黃氏。嚴侍下，弟瀠、沂、濟、澄，娶蔡氏。福建鄉試第十一名，會試第二百四十一名。
translation_en:
Zhang Rong, courtesy name Congfan, was registered in a military household of the Left Imperial Bodyguard and was a native of Dongming County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ben, his grandfather Lin, and his father Zi; his father's former wife was Lady Li, and his mother was Lady Mi. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yu and his younger brother Zhao. He married Lady Liu. He placed fifteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Ang, courtesy name Deyi, was registered in a civilian household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji, his grandfather Xian〔granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations〕, and his father Kuan; his father's former wife was Lady Ma, and his mother was Lady Zheng. Parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Sheng, and his younger brothers were Mian, Yu, and Bing. He married Lady Chen. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Le, courtesy name Xieqing, was registered in a military household in Fushan County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanbin〔posthumously appointed Prefect〕; his grandfather was Yu〔Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, posthumously awarded the titles Grand Master for Proper Service (zhengfeng dafu) and Minister for Orthodox Governance (zhengzhi qing)〕; his father was Yan〔Vice Director of the Office of Imperial Seals〕; and his mother was Lady Li〔granted the title Lady (ruren)〕. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Qi〔an Imperial University student〕, Gai, and Fei〔a jinshi of the same examination year〕. The transcription here contains “pol” [?]. His younger brothers were Jie, Tang, Guo, Bing, Ru, Li, and Zhuo. He married Lady Li and subsequently Lady Xie. He placed seventy-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Chao, courtesy name Junxin, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Keyu, his grandfather Ziyun, and his father Kai; his mother was Lady Yang, and his stepmother was Lady Huang. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Ying, Yi, Ji, and Cheng. He married Lady Cai. He placed eleventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dong Qi 董琦, courtesy name Tiancui, was registered in a civilian household in Yangxin County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A county government student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Ziyou; his father, Yi, a Police Chief; and his mother, née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jue, Hu, and Lian, and his wife was née Wang. He placed seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zong 楊總, courtesy name Keping, was registered with the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and came from Fangshan County, Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the eleventh day of the intercalary second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dechun; his grandfather, Qing; his father, Li, a Company Commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; and his mother, née Tian. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tong, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Ji. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently married women née Wang and née Liu. He placed 106th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Fang 高淓, courtesy name Yingzhi, was registered in a military household in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhi, was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. His grandfather, Heng, was granted the title Director in the Ministry of Revenue and posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. His father, Quan, held the titles Grand Master for Proper Counsel and Governor for Assisting Governance and served as Right Vice Minister of Works in Nanjing. His mother, née Xu, was granted the title Lady of Virtue. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Han; Ji, a Director in the Ministry of Works; Huai and He, Imperial University students; Zhu; Ying; Jun; Qi, an Office Vice Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; and Xiang. His younger brothers were Tong, Can, Jing, and Yong. His wife was née Yang. He placed 230th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Qing 馬卿, courtesy name Jingchen, was registered in a civilian household in Lin County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, an Assistant Prefect; his grandfather, Lin; his father, Tu, a County Magistrate; and his mother, née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yu, and his wife was née Wang. He placed thirteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Yusheng, registered in a military household in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Qijin, he ranked seventh in family order, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Dun, was an Assistant Magistrate; his father was Wei and his mother was née Zheng, both living; his elder brother was Yuchun, his younger brother was Yuchang, and his wife was née Yao; he placed fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Wen, registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Huanzhang, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged fifty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jishan; his grandfather was Si'an; his father, Guang, was a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his mother was née Wang, and his father was deceased while his mother was living; his younger brother was Xianda, he married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Zhang, and he placed seventy-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 100th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Lian, registered in a military household in Jiyang County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, and originally from Yuci County, Shanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xizhou, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yu, was a Police Chief; his grandfather was Tai; his father, Gang, was an Assistant Magistrate; his mother was née Zhu and his stepmother was née Wu; both parents were recorded as living, his younger brothers were Qi and Zhu, his wife was née Wang, and he placed thirty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yan, registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xianke, he ranked seventh in family order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the eleventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziying; his grandfather was Decheng; his father was Gonghu and his mother was née Zhan, both living; his younger brother was Botan, his wife was née Weng, and he placed twenty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Biao, courtesy name Minwang, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather, Xian, was a Judge; his father was Gong, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Zheng and Jian, and his wife was née Liu. He ranked seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Maoyuan, courtesy name Shanzhang, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xingren; his grandfather was Zi; his father was Cheng, and his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Maoxun, Maoshi, and Maoyu, and his wife was née Li. He ranked second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Jue, courtesy name Yuzhang, was registered in a civilian household in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiong; his grandfather was Zongli; his father was Da, and his mother was née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Zhen, and his younger brothers were Zhu, Xin, and Wan. His first wife was née Huang, and his subsequent wife was née Dai. He ranked forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Li, courtesy name Guozheng, was registered in a military household in Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiyong; his grandfather, Yiming, held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; his father, Xian, was a Vice Prefect, and his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Wu. He ranked 105th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yuan Jing, registered in Qing County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zaidao, he ranked first in birth order, and he was thirty years old, born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Cong, his father Heng, and his mother née Fan; both parents were living, his wife was née Hu, and he placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

An Pan, registered in Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Hongjian, he ranked first in birth order, and he was twenty-seven years old, born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, Assistant Administration Commissioner in Yunnan, his grandfather Weimin, his father You, a tribute scholar, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Zheng; his parents and at least one grandparent were living, his younger brothers were Shuo, Li, and Yan, his wife was née Cheng, and he placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Wan, registered in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Buzhi, he ranked third in birth order, and he was twenty-nine years old, born on the seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingde, his grandfather Yanzhang, his father Sheng, and his mother née Jiang; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Fu, Xuan, and Kuan, his younger brothers Chong, Jun, Huan, Ning, and Cha, his wife was née Yuan, and he placed fifty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shi, registered in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jingzhang, he ranked seventh in birth order, and he was thirty-seven years old, born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Zhong, his father Wan, a county school Instructor, his father's former wife née Hu, his mother née Yu, and his stepmother née Pan; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Nan, Chun, Xiang, Liang, Mu, and Cai, his younger brothers Tang, Shan, and Biao, his wife was née Yang, and he placed fifty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Mu Konghui, registered in Tangyi County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Boqian, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-seven, born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Biao; his father was Qing; his mother was née Ren, and his stepmother née Huang. His parents and members of the grandparental generation were living; his younger brothers were Kongyao, Kongshi, Kongzhao, Kongyang, Kongfang, Kongxuan, and Kongshu, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Rui, registered in Jizhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yinglin, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-eight, born on the thirtieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Su, an Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Zongben, Magistrate of Linchuan County; his father was Zhen, a Department Magistrate; his mother was née Li and his birth mother née Cui, both granted the title Lady for Service. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Yun, Xiu, Peng (a County Magistrate), and □ [?], and his younger brothers were Zhen and others whose names are illegible (□□□□□□) [?]. His first wife was née Li, and his subsequent wife née Fu. He placed eleventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Nusheng, registered in Changting County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhenfu, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was thirty-six, born on the second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanshi, posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Ju, a Prefectural School Instructor; his father's name is illegible (□□□), and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Shentang, the names of his younger brothers are illegible (□□□□) [?], and his wife was née Yi. He placed ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Pu, registered in Yanling County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to an artisan household and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yiqing, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-two, born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather was Yongqing; his father was Quan; and his mother was née Cheng. His parents and members of the grandparental generation were living; his younger brother was Pang, and he was betrothed to a woman née Zhao. He placed forty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tao Ji 陶驥, courtesy name Liangbo, was registered in a military household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Meng, was an Assistant Prefect with the prestige title fengxun dafu; and his father, Yongchun, was an Associate Prefect promoted to the prestige rank chaolie dafu. His father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Lin, was a Clerk. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked twenty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Duo 閻鐸, courtesy name Daoming, was registered in a civilian household in Guo County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twelfth day of the second month. His great-grandfather's name is illegible (□); his grandfather, Guan, was a government student; his father's name is illegible (□□); and his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His younger brother's name is illegible (□□). He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zan 劉瓚, courtesy name Chaozhong, was registered in a military household of Huichuan Guard under the Sichuan Regional Military Commission, and his family originated in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather's name is illegible (□□); his grandfather was Changzong; his father's name is illegible (□□); and his mother was née Ai. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yu, a County Vice Magistrate, and Jing; his younger brother's name is illegible (□). He married a woman née Chen. He ranked seventieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yueyin 王曰印, courtesy name Zhongyong, was registered in a civilian household in Guang'an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wengui; his grandfather was Ming; his father was Jigang; and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Ao and Xiao. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Yang, courtesy name Yixiu, was registered in a civilian household in Zaoqiang County, Jizhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizhong; his grandfather, Daliang; and his father, Fang. His father's former wives were née Li and née Hao, and his mother was née Lu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Chao, Jin, Yue, and Huang, and his younger brothers were Zhuo and Xuan. He married a woman née Lü. He placed one hundredth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Teng Yuan, courtesy name Shiyi, was registered in a military household of Jiyang Guard and was a native of Jian'an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Changyi; his grandfather, Wenshou; and his father, Yue. His father's former wives were née Ling and née Wang, and his mother was née Chang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chen, Xun, and Xun, and his younger brother was Kui. He married a woman née Lin and subsequently a woman née Dong. He placed one hundred eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Hong, courtesy name Bodu, was registered in a civilian household in Yangjiang County, Zhaoqing Prefecture, Guangdong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather, Ning, a Records Examiner; and his father, Fang, a Registrar. His mother was née Xu, with the title “Confucian Lady” [?; the transcription reads 儒人, probably intended as 孺人, “Lady”]. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jing and Yi. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Lin. He placed seventy-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Gang, courtesy name Zhengzhi, was registered in an artisan household in Jinhua County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenda, initially granted the posthumous title of Investigating Censor and subsequently that of Surveillance Vice Commissioner; his grandfather was Xiang, a Surveillance Assistant Commissioner; his father was Shao; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Ji, Jing, Lun, Ji, Xiu, Chun, Wei, and Wan. He married a woman née Li. He placed thirty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred first in the Metropolitan Examination.

蕭世賢〔貫直隸安慶府桐城縣，民籍，江西泰和縣人，縣學附學生，治書經，字君正，行一，年二十六，十一月初一日生〕。曾祖旭衡，祖仁本〔縣丞〕，父俊彥，母劉氏。具慶下，弟世和、世寧、世泰、世義、世友，娶劉氏。應天府鄉試第七名，會試第九十二名。

黃鞏〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯固，行一，年二十六，十一月初一日生〕。曾祖師憲，祖文嘉，父德珍，前母陳氏，母鄭氏。慈侍下，弟孚、鼙，娶林氏。福建鄉試第七名，會試第一百十三名。

雷啓東〔貫河南開封府儀封縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字震之，行一，年三十一，十二月初四日生〕。曾祖遇春，祖昇，父文〔教諭〕，母楊氏。具慶下，娶杜氏。河南鄉試第七十二名，會試第九十一名。
translation_en:
Wang Jiao 王教, courtesy name Danfu, was registered in a civilian household in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yungong; his grandfather, Gang, was a Magistrate; and his father, Yan, was a Chief Judicial Officer in a princely establishment. His legal mothers were Lady Liao and Lady Wang, and his birth mother was Lady Huang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Xu, and he married Lady Li. He placed fourteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Shixian 蕭世賢, courtesy name Junzheng, was registered in a civilian household in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was originally from Taihe County, Jiangxi. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuheng; his grandfather, Renben, was a County Vice Magistrate; his father was Junyan, and his mother was Lady Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shihe, Shining, Shitai, Shiyi, and Shiyou, and he married Lady Liu. He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Gong 黃鞏, courtesy name Bogu, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shixian; his grandfather was Wenjia; his father was Dezhen; his father's former wife was Lady Chen, and his mother was Lady Zheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Fu and Pi [?], and he married Lady Lin. He placed seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei Qidong 雷啓東, courtesy name Zhenzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Yifeng County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuchun; his grandfather was Sheng; his father, Wen, was a county-school Instructor; and his mother was Lady Yang. Both parents were living. He married Lady Du. He placed seventy-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

張思齊〔貫湖廣黃州府蘄州軍籍，國子生，治書經，字希賢，行二，年三十五，八月二十日生〕。曾祖珍，祖通〔知縣〕，父文〔通判〕，母陳氏〔封孺人〕。永感下，兄濯，弟堯、思舜、思臯、思夔，娶宋氏。湖廣鄉試第四名，會試第二百九十二名。
translation_en:
Wang Yi, registered in a military household in Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Leping County, Shanxi. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tianyu. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-third day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Fu, Chief Astrologer; his grandfather was Ying, a Subprefectural Judge; his father was Ze, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His wife was née Li. He placed fourteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Han, registered in a military household of the Tengxiang Right Guard and originally from the Guangning Rear Garrison Guard in Liaodong, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruzhen. He was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Fushan, his grandfather Wang, his father Yun, and his mother née Liu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were He, Hui, and Xi, and his wife was née Cheng. He placed eighty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Shiyong, registered in a military household in Jiaohe County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziji. He was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Youliang, his grandfather Gang, and his father Rang, whose title is transcribed as Haoqi wei [?]. His father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zan, and his wife was née Luo. He placed eighty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Siqi, registered in a military household in Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xixian. He was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather was Tong, a County Magistrate; his father was Wen, an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Chen, who had been granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zhuo; his younger brothers were Yao, Sishun, Sigao, and Sikui; and his wife was née Song. He placed fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Guang, courtesy name Chongzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zixiang, his grandfather Hai, his father Wen, and his mother Lady Lu; his mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Pu and his younger brother Bo. He married Lady Zhang and subsequently Lady Xia. He placed fifty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Ai, courtesy name Zifang, was registered in a civilian household in Shangrao County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was eighteenth in birth order, aged forty, and born on the fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cunwu, his grandfather Xinchun, and his father Yue; his father's former wife was Lady Wang, and his mother was Lady Wu. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Ru and his younger brother Ying. He married Lady Han and subsequently Lady Hu. He placed forty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Yingxiang, courtesy name Weixian, was registered in a civilian household in Changxing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Changzhou County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huaide, his grandfather Daming, his father Chang, and his mother Lady Yang; both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingzhen, and his younger brothers were Yingkui and Yingyuan. He married Lady Zhang. He placed seventy-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhishu, courtesy name Kequan, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the nineteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yungong, his grandfather Kun, and his father Fang, an Assistant Prefect; his father's former wife was Lady Zheng, his mother was Lady Huang, and his stepmother was Lady Hu. He had living parents and at least one living grandparent. His younger brothers were Zhiji, Zhiye, and Zhixian. He married Lady Li. He placed eighty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Su Ming, registered in a civilian household in Longqing Subprefecture in the directly administered territory and originating from Changping County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Imperial University who specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shiyuan; he was first in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the twelfth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was De, his grandfather Yi, and his father Rong, a Registrar; his mother was née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Zhao and Wei. He married a woman née Ding and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed 113th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Minzhi, registered in a civilian household in Ying Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Imperial University who specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zishi; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Ju [annotation illegible: □□], and his father Hu [annotation illegible: □□]; his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Min’an, and his younger brothers were Min□ and Minbiao. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed 40th in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Gao, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered territory and originating from Shanghai County, was a Confucian scholar who specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shunchen; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Sizong, his grandfather Gongliang [annotation illegible: □□], and his father You, an honorary official. His legal mother was née Xu, and his birth mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother’s name is illegible (□); his younger brothers are listed as □□ [name or names illegible; division uncertain], Lu, Yue, Zhou, and Xia. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed 3rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 72nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Pu, registered in a military household in Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University who specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhongmei; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yancheng, his grandfather Hua, and his father Sheng, a County Vice Magistrate. His father’s former wife was née Sun, his mother née Luo, and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xi and Bi. He married a woman née Liao. He placed 50th in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 62nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Sheng 孫勝 was registered in a military household in Fenghua County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Minzhong; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Weiyao, his grandfather Zhizhong, his father Huimao, and his mother née Cheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yu and Pi [?], and his younger brother was Lun; his wife was née Ruan. He ranked sixty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Peiling 李培齡 was registered in a military household of the Jinwu Front Guard and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Renshou; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather Wen held the military prestige title Commandant of Manifest Trust (zhaoxin xiaowei); his father Wei was an Assistant Commander; and his mother, née Du, had been granted the title Lady of Respect (gongren). His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His wife was née Zhai. He ranked fifty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ju 劉舉 was registered in a civilian household in Lulong County, Yongping Prefecture, Zhili, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Shida; he was first in birth order, apparently aged thirty-two [the preceding two characters are illegible], and born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Shitong, his grandfather Ying, and his father Shou; his father's former wife was née Du, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Sheng and □; he married a woman née Wei and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He ranked sixty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ximeng 王希孟 was registered in a civilian household in Huojia County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongzhe; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the eleventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shi'er, his grandfather Jing, and his father An; his father's former wife was née Yuan, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Xu. He ranked seventy-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Yu, of Nanzheng County, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi, was registered in a military artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Boxiang. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Wei; his grandfather, Ning; and his father, Guang, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Deng, and his stepmother née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhu, Chong, Han, Ao, Ke, He, 𦐥 (reading uncertain [?]), and Yi. His wife was née Lü. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Biao, of Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, had an illegible household registration category [?] and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name is illegible [?]. Second in birth order, with the following three characters illegible [?], he was born on the thirteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Chengzhong; his grandfather, Mengqiao; and his father's name is illegible [?]. His mother was née Zhuang. Both parents were living. Three further characters are illegible [?]. His wife's surname is illegible [?]. His rank in the Fujian Provincial Examination is illegible [?]; he ranked 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Peng, of Hongya County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name is illegible [?]. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, whose name is illegible [?], was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor. His father's name is illegible [?], and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were E, Yuan, and Yan. His wife was née Zhan. He ranked fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Zhongdao, of Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Congzhi. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and was born on the second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Sui, a Police Chief; his grandfather was Yu, an Assistant Instructor granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue. His father was Shixian, a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites (the character 木 in the title is doubtful [?]). His mother, née Zeng, was granted the title Lady (ruren). His parents and grandparental generation were living. His younger brothers were Zhongfu, Zhonghong, Zhongyou, Zhongxi, and Zhonghan. His wife was née Huang. He ranked fifty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gu Tang, registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Liang’ai; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenchang; his grandfather, Qiong, and father, Hao, had each been granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations; his mother was née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Liang, and his younger brothers were Can, Rou, and Li. He married a woman née Lu. He placed ninetieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Rujin, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xiwu; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-three, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zijia [annotation illegible: □□□□]; his grandfather, Shen, was Prefect of Wenzhou; his father, Qianheng, was Vice Director of the Office of Messengers and was posthumously granted an illegible title [□□]; his mother was née Lin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xiying, a District Magistrate, Xida, and Xishao; his younger brothers were Sui [?], Xihuo, Ruyu, and Ruzhuo. He married a woman née Chen. He placed fifty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Bobian, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yinghe; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the seventeenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jidao; his grandfather was Zirong; his father was □jue, with the first character illegible; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Boti and Boshu. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed forty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Yong, registered in a civilian household in Luoshan County, Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Mingqing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shaozong; his grandfather was Zhen; his father was Jihui; and his mother was née Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Tong and Zhou. He married a woman née Wan. He placed seventy-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Chun, registered in an artisan household in Miyun County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dehou, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather, Jian, received the honorary appointment of Archivist in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his father, Ju, held the honorary title of Righteous Official; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Ze, Shu, and Cang, the last a metropolitan examination graduate (gongshi); his wife was née Wang. He placed 124th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Yu, registered in an officer household of the Yunnan Right Guard in Yunnan and originally from Changzhou County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yongcheng, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather's name is illegible (□□), as is his father's (□); his mother was née Gu, and his stepmother was née Yuan. Both parents were living; the name or names of his elder brother or brothers are illegible (□□) [?], and his younger brothers were Kai, Chu, and Xuan; his wife was née Shi. He placed fifteenth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhang, registered in a commoner household in Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ying□ [?], he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Dun, was a District Magistrate; his grandfather's and father's names are each illegible (□); and his mother was née Zhuo. His mother alone was living; the name or names of his younger brother or brothers are illegible (□□) [?]; his wife was née Zheng. He placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Yu, registered in a commoner household in Yongfeng County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhuozhi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Wenduo, was posthumously appointed a Vice Director; his grandfather, Zhang, was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Gu, and his mother was née Zou. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Ji, and his younger brothers were Huai, Fa, Long, and one whose name is illegible (□); his wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.
