translation_en:
Wang Zimo 王子謨 was registered in a civilian household in Chun’an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Rugao. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-nine and was born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benzong, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his grandfather was Zhishan, granted the honorary title of Investigating Censor; and his father was Bin, a Prefect. His mother, née Zhang, was granted the title of Lady of Respect by imperial patent. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ziyan, a Vice Director; his younger brothers were Zixun and Zijin. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Chongxiao 胡冲霄 was registered in a civilian household in Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Pengju. His birth order is recorded as 的 [?]. He was aged thirty-six and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather’s name is illegible (□), as is his grandfather’s (□□); his father was Neng, and his mother was née Xing. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chonghan and Chongyun. He married a woman née Lu and subsequently a woman née Dong. He placed fiftieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Min 閔, whose given name is illegible (□), was registered in a civilian household in Ren County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a student of the Imperial University. His classical specialization (□□), courtesy name (□□), and birth order (□) are illegible. He was aged twenty-six and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather’s name is illegible (□); his father was Zongru, and his mother was née Bian. Both parents were living. The following four characters are illegible (□□□□). He married a woman née Zhu. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Zi 彭滋 was registered in a civilian household in Shangcheng County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yizhi. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-nine and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junjie; his grandfather was Youlin; and his father was Yue, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions. His mother was née Yu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yongshou, Yongchang, Ji, Jiang, and Yang; his younger brothers were Shu and Ying. He married a woman née Yu. He placed fifteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wei Qi, courtesy name Qiaoyi, was registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ziyu was a magistrate; his grandfather was Chonghong; his father Mo was a magistrate; and his mother was née Xiong. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Gai, Fei, and Bing, and his wife was née Xiong. He placed sixty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Yuan, courtesy name Shanzhang, was registered in a civilian household in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather, whose name is illegible, was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. His grandfather’s and father’s names and official annotations are illegible. His mother, née Xiao, and stepmother, née Hu, were each granted the title Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. The sibling list reads “elder brother(s) Heng Tai; younger brother(s) Zhen Yuan Heng Shi” [?]. His wife was née Yi. He placed 106th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ding, courtesy name Daqi, was from Wucheng County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Dengzhou Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhiming; his grandfather is recorded as Liang□□ [?]; and his father Shan was a magistrate. His legal mother was née Liu, and his birth mother was née Chu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ang and one whose name is illegible; his younger brothers were one whose name is illegible, Hui, and another whose name is illegible [?]. His wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was also née Wang. He placed third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xuan, courtesy name Yantong, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bo; his grandfather Nian and father Qiu were both assistant instructors; and his mother was née Wang. His parents and grandparent(s) were living. His younger brother was Zong, and his wife was née Chen. He placed thirtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xie Guobiao 謝國表 was registered in a military household of Zhenwu Guard and was a native of Daizhou, Shanxi. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Minzhan, ranked first among his brothers, and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather, Duo, was a prefectural judge; his father, Xi, was a subprefect; and his mother was née Feng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Guozhao, a tribute student (gongshi), Guozheng, and Guopin. His wife was née Wu. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Kewen 張克溫 was registered in an artisan household in Linfen County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Dehe, ranked second among his brothers, and was twenty-four years old [?], born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yao; his grandfather’s name is illegible (□□); his father was Ren; and his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Keming. He married a woman née Du and subsequently a woman née He. He placed sixteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Gao 師臯 was registered in a civilian household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zhifu, ranked first among his brothers, and was twenty-one years old, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather’s name is illegible (□); his father, Yi, was a tribute student (gongshi); and his mother was née Tian. Both parents were living. His younger brothers are recorded as Kui 蘷 and Kui 夔 [?]. His wife was née Zhao. He placed twenty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Yunxiao 殷雲霄 was registered in a civilian household in Shouzhang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Jinfu, ranked first among his brothers, and was twenty-six years old, born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Duo, had been granted the privilege of wearing an official cap and girdle under applicable regulations; and his father, Qi, was a county magistrate. His legal mother was née Zhang, his stepmother née Ren, and his birth mother née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Yunni. His wife was née Yue. He placed fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Hu 葉鵠, courtesy name Shiju, was registered in Shangrao County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fortieth [?] in family birth order and was thirty years old, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Zhixian, his father Qiong, and his mother née Ding. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Peng, E, and Yue; his younger brothers were Qi, Lin, Feng, He, and Huang. He married a woman née Mao and subsequently a woman née Cheng. He placed fourteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Wen 馬文, courtesy name Zaidao, was registered in Jinchi Command, Yunnan, in a military household. An additional student at the command school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked third in family birth order and was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Gui, his father Cheng, his mother née Zhu, and his stepmother née Cui. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brother was □, and his younger brother was Wu. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Shaoxian 孫紹先, courtesy name Ruzong, was registered in Zhenwu Guard, Shanxi, in a military household and was a native of Daizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture. A Daizhou government school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first in family birth order and was twenty-three years old [?; the age formula is garbled], born on the twenty-third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cai, his grandfather Sheng, his father Zhang (a department magistrate), and his mother née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His younger brothers were Shaofang, Shaowen, Shaokui, Shaoke, Shaoli, Shaozhong, Shaolie, Shaoxian 紹賢, and Shaozhe. He married a woman née Tian. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shouda 劉守達, courtesy name Yingzheng, was registered in Kaizhou, Daming Prefecture, in the Directly Administered Region, in a civilian household. An additional student at the department government school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second in family birth order and was twenty-six years old, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun, his grandfather He, his father Xi, and his mother née Fu. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brother was Shouqiong, and his younger brother was Shoujie. He married a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Qing, registered in a military household in Fushan County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Mingqing. Third in birth order, he was thirty-six years old and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanbin, posthumously granted the title of Prefect; his grandfather was Yu, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, posthumously granted the prestige titles Zhengfeng dafu and Zhengzhi qing; and his father was Ke, formerly Left Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. His legal mother, née Zhang, was granted the title Lady (ruren); his birth mother was née Fan. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Fei, an Imperial University student. His younger brothers were Rong, Luan (a jinshi of the same year), Ju, Bing, Guo, Fei, Mi, Su, and Nie [the transcription includes “cf” before this list; the names are uncertain in places]. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Yu. He ranked forty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two-hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yi, registered in a military household in Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name is illegible (□□). Second in birth order, he was thirty-two years old and was born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; the names of his grandfather and father and his mother's maiden surname are illegible (□ each). His stepmother was née Liang. Both parents were living. His elder brother's name is illegible (□), as is the text naming his younger brother or brothers (□□). He married a woman née Fan. His rank in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination is illegible (□□□); his Metropolitan Examination rank is partially illegible (□□一, ending in one).

Chen Huai, registered in a civilian household in an illegible county (□□) of an illegible prefecture (□□), Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name is illegible (□□). The text giving his birth order, and possibly his age, is illegible (□□□) [?]. He was born on the twentieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dao□; the names of his grandfather and father are illegible (□ each). His mother was née Lin. Both parents were deceased. The text naming his elder brother or brothers is illegible (□□□□). He married a woman née Fan. His rank in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination is illegible (□□); he ranked forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Wenxiang, registered in a military household in Baling County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shiheng. First in birth order, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Jian, and his father Han. His father's former wife was née Jiang, and his mother was née Lu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Wenkui. He married a woman née He. He ranked fifteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one-hundred-and-seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chang Zai 常在, courtesy name Shoude, was registered in Yushe County, Liao Subprefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng, granted the honorary title of Supervising Secretary and posthumously awarded that of Prefect; his grandfather was Xian, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his father was Jing, a County Magistrate. His mother was née Qiao, and his stepmothers were née Shen and née Guo. His mother alone of his parents was living. His younger brothers were Zhi, Cheng, Shu, and Zeng. He married a woman née Li and subsequently another woman née Li. He placed fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Tai 杜泰, courtesy name Mengzhan, was registered in Changqing County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. A county government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Keming, his grandfather Zi, and his father Shi; his mother was née Feng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hua, Heng, Huo, and Yi. He married a woman née Hao. He placed ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yue Hu 樂頀, courtesy name Mingyin, was registered in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked eleventh among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiheng, his grandfather Xiangchun, and his father Dacheng. His father's former wife was née Liu, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shao and Hu 護, and his younger brother was Ying. He married a woman née Zhan. He placed forty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Jianzhong 董建中, courtesy name Shangmin, was registered in Shouzhang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. A county government student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ge, his grandfather Quan, and his father Cong, an Imperial University student. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shizhong and Daozhong, and his younger brothers were Dazhong, Yongzhong, and Zhizhong. He married a woman née Lü. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Shi, courtesy name Zijing, was registered in a military household in Yingcheng County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather, Xiang; his father, Dazhong, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Zhou. Both parents were living. His wife was née Xu. He placed fifty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yanrui, courtesy name Yuancheng, was registered in a civilian household in Ji County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twentieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo; his grandfather, Jie, a Salt Distribution Commissioner; his father, Ji, a Left Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; and his mother, née Duan, who had been granted the title Lady (ruren). His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Yanqing, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Yanzuo. His wife was née Guo; he subsequently married a woman née Cui. He placed sixty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shiqing, courtesy name Xixian, was registered in a civilian household in Changning County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuchun; his grandfather, Guicong; his father, Chen; and his mother, née Luo. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Shiyan, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed forty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Lun, courtesy name Tingyan, was registered in a civilian household in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Da, a Prefect; his grandfather, Ning, who was designated Worthy, Good, Upright, and Correct; and his father, Guang, a Registrar. His father’s former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Yue. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ji, and his younger brothers were Xu and Jin. His wife was née Wang. He placed 116th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Hao, courtesy name Ziyuan, was registered in a military household of Yongzhou Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Changzhou County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guan, his grandfather Qing, and his father Jing; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Lüqiu. He placed fifty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ni Zhang, courtesy name Xianfu, was registered in an artisan household of Wanping County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Wu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benyi, his grandfather Gongjue, and his father Zhen; his father's former wife was née Bao, and his mother was née Fang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Gui, Jin, Zan, Xu, and Jian, the last a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites. He married a woman née Chen. He placed fiftieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jiuzhang, courtesy name Zhenyi, was registered in a civilian household of Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-six, born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shineng, his grandfather Min, and his father Kaiwan; his mother was née Lu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Jiuyi. He married a woman née Wu. He placed sixty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yong, courtesy name Shunzhong, was registered in a salt-producing household of Raoping County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangwen, his grandfather Bangning, and his father Yuanyu; his legal mother was née Shen, and his birth mother was née Zheng. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Xian, Xing, Xuan, and Jie. He married a woman née Chen. He placed second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Jing, courtesy name Tianxu, was registered in a military household in Shenyang Central Guard, Liaodong, and was a native of Yangxin County, Wuding Subprefecture, Ji’nan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Duan; his grandfather, Sheng, had been granted the honorary cap and girdle under applicable regulations; his father was Jie; his mother was née Yu, and his stepmother née Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xiu, and his wife was née Chen. He placed tenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Zongtai, courtesy name Leshan, was registered in a civilian household in Qingyuan County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged fifty, and born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zeng; his grandfather, Jian, was a Registrar; his father was Xuan; his mother was née Song, and his stepmother née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Zonglu, and his wife was née Li. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Wenbi, courtesy name Liangyu, was registered in a civilian household in Guiyang County, Chenzhou Subprefecture, Huguang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Siqian, was a District Magistrate; his grandfather, Ke, was a Judge; his father was Shoucheng, and his mother was née He. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Wenxi, and his younger brothers were Wenying, Wenban, Wenkui, and Wenlong. His wife was née Ou; he subsequently married a woman née Gao. He placed forty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Fan, courtesy name Juefu, was registered in a civilian household in Yuncheng County, Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Cong, held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; his father, Long, was an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Fan. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Shi and Zhen, and his wife was née Hou. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

潘棠〔貫湖廣辰州衛軍籍，直隸寧國府太平縣人，國子生，治詩經，字希召，行二，年三十三，十二月二十四日生。〕曾祖九成，祖鏞，父汰〔正七品散官〕，母傅氏。具慶下。兄材，弟林、桂、槐、梅、相。娶張氏。湖廣鄉試第五十一名，會試第四十五名。

汪和〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字惟節，行十，年三十，十月初十日生。〕曾祖彥端〔縣丞〕，祖勉〔貢士〕，父洋，前母蘇氏，母嚴氏，繼母楊氏。重慶下。兄榮〔義官〕、森、泰〔義官〕、諫、槩、棐，弟朴、梓、桌、橿。娶董氏。浙江鄉試第四十二名，會試第一百十一名。

胡汝楫〔貫陝西寧夏中衛軍籍，應天府溧陽縣人，國子生，治易經，字濟之，行二，年三十八，正月二十二日生。〕曾祖士真，祖雄，父璉〔贈戶部員外郎〕，母陳氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下。兄汝礪〔知府〕，弟汝霖、汝明〔義官〕、汝翼。娶茅氏。陝西鄉試第二十五名，會試第一百八十三名。

劉田〔貫山東兗州府東平州東阿縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯耕，行一，年二十五，正月二十七日生。〕曾祖璉〔教諭〕，祖觀〔承事郎，贈吏部郎中〕，父約〔參政〕，母徐氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下。弟谷、隅、階、牧、垣。娶蘇氏。山東鄉試第五十七名，會試第二百十九名。
translation_en:
Pan Tang, courtesy name Xizhao, was registered in a military household of Chenzhou Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Taiping County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jiucheng; his grandfather, Yong; his father, Tai, held a prestige title of the primary seventh rank; and his mother was née Fu; both parents were living; his elder brother was Cai and his younger brothers were Lin, Gui, Huai, Mei, and Xiang; his wife was née Zhang; he placed fifty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang He, courtesy name Weijie, was registered in a civilian household of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was tenth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yanduan, a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather, Mian, was a tribute student; his father was Yang; his father's former wife was née Su, his mother was née Yan, and his stepmother was née Yang; his parents and at least one grandparent were living; his elder brothers were Rong, an honorary official, Sen, Tai, an honorary official, Jian, Gai, and Fei, and his younger brothers were Pu, Zi, Zhuo [?], and Jiang; his wife was née Dong; he placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Ruji, courtesy name Jizhi, was registered in a military household of Ningxia Central Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture; a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Shizhen; his grandfather, Xiong; his father, Lian, was posthumously appointed a Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his mother, née Chen, was granted the title Lady of Suitability; his mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brother was Ruli, a Prefect, and his younger brothers were Rulin, Ruming, an honorary official, and Ruyi; his wife was née Mao; he placed twenty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tian, courtesy name Bogeng, was registered in a civilian household of Dong'e County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong; a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Lian, an Instructor; his grandfather, Guan, held the title Gentleman for Rendering Service and was posthumously appointed a Director in the Ministry of Personnel; his father, Yue, was an Administration Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Xu, was granted the title Lady of Suitability; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Gu, Yu, Jie, Mu, and Yuan; his wife was née Su; he placed fifty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Kuan 賀寬, registered in a civilian household in Yongxin County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Maofu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Benning, his grandfather Xundao, and his father Jian, an honorary official; his mother was née Zhou. His parents and a grandparent were living. His elder brother was Hong, and his younger brothers were Cai, Chong, Shen, Cha, Yu, Ning [?], Song, and Mi. He married a woman née Yin. He placed forty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Ying 吳盈, registered in a civilian household in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zichi; he was thirty-eighth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the eleventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Delong, his grandfather Daoyuan, and his father Bo, a prefectural school instructor. His father’s principal wife was née Xu, and his birth mother was née Wang. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Lin, a magistrate; Ji; Lou; and Tan, a registrar. His younger brothers were Rong and Zi. He married a woman née Cao. He placed eighty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Yi 丁儀, registered in a salt-producing household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenfan; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Shifu, his grandfather Zou□ [?], and his father Chaobin; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother’s name is illegible (□□). He married a woman née Li. He placed thirty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Suo Chengxue 索承學, registered in a military household in Pizhou, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xunfu; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Jing, a county school instructor, and his father Kui; his mother was née Wei. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Qinxue and Haoxue. He married a woman née Hu. He placed forty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Su Min 蘇民, courtesy name Tianxiu, was registered in a guardsman household of the Ceremonial Guard Office in Shaanxi and was a native of Suichang County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was thirty years old, born on the fourteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Rengui, his father Wentong, and his mother née Zhao. His father was deceased and his mother living; he married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yue 陳鉞, courtesy name Dewei, was registered in a military household in Fengyang County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first in his family and was forty-one years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Jing, his father Zhang, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Quan, Gang, Jian, Zhao, Qin, Zhen, Tang, and Zhu; he married a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Cong 黃琮, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was registered in an artisan household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Le'an County, Jiangxi. A student of the Yingtian prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in his family and was thirty-six years old, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongmin, his grandfather Boyi, his father Duhao, and his mother née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Gongxian, Qiong, and Ying; he married a woman née Yan. He placed tenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yi Shugao 易舒誥, courtesy name Qinzhi, was registered in a postal-relay household in You County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked sixth in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yao, his grandfather Xian, his father Wanfu (granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations), and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shuhan; he married a woman née Xiao. He placed forty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ma Xun 馬馴, courtesy name Defu, was registered in a civilian household in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong; he was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked first in family order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Cong, and his father Neng, a County Vice Magistrate; his mother, née Wang, was still living, while his father was deceased; his younger brother was Tong, and he married a woman née Liu; he placed 125th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Lianggui 江良貴, courtesy name Rusi, was registered in a civilian household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi; he was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, ranked eleventh in family order, and was aged thirty-four, born on the eleventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuncong, his grandfather Chang, a County Magistrate, and his father Yu; his father's former wife was née Li and his mother née Deng; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Liangzhou, an Imperial University student, Liangben, Liangyi, Liangcang, an Assistant Instructor, Lianghai, and Liangjun, an honorary official; his younger brothers were Liangcai, Liangtian, and Liangji; he married a woman née Zhan and placed thirtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Ren 周任, courtesy name Yiren, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked seventh in family order, and was aged thirty-seven, born on the sixth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, an Imperial University student, his grandfather Jingchang, and his father Liang; his mother was née Mao, and both parents were deceased; his younger brothers were Ben, Ji, Song, and Yue; he married a woman née Xu and subsequently another woman née Xu; he placed eighty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Lianghan 陳良翰, courtesy name Jingshen, was registered in a military household in Luojiang County, Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan; he was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked ninth in family order, and was aged thirty-three, born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuzu, his grandfather Yingfu, and his father Ang, a Registrar; his father's former wife was née Huang and his mother née Wang; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Liangfu, Lianggui, Liangmao, Liangshou, Liangchen, Liangfu, Liangzhong, and Liangxu; he married a woman née Cheng and placed twenty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fang Xianke, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shuxian, and he ranked third in the family. He was twenty-one years old, born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shihong; his grandfather, Yongzhong; his father, Sui, a School Instructor; and his mother, née Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Guike and Maoke. He was betrothed to a woman née Zou. He placed second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jie, registered in Jinyun County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Chaoxin, and he ranked nineteenth in the family. He was twenty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tang, Vice Minister of Justice; his grandfather, Hun, a National University student; his father, Jin; and his mother, née Ying. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Bo, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his younger brothers were Yuan, Jin, Jing, and Hu. He married a woman née Chen. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Ding, registered in Jixi County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jingfu, and he ranked second in the family. He was thirty-two years old, born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanzhao; his grandfather, Wenshan; his father, Yuqian; and his mother, née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Hong, and his younger brothers were Ning, Rou (宍) [?], and Yin. He married a woman née Hu. He placed sixty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jin, registered in Taiping County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Chongzhi, and he ranked eleventh in the family. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Renxun; his grandfather, Honghui; his father, Maoyang; and his mother, née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xiao and Ce. He married a woman née Xia. He placed twenty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Chong, registered in a military household in Taixing County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Pengju, he was second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the eighteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, a prefect; his grandfather was Lin; his father was Fu, an assistant magistrate; and his mother was née Cai. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Yu, a tribute scholar; his younger brothers were Fei, Cui, Qiao, Hong, Xu (诩), Ke, Ao, Han, Jian, Bang, Qu, Xi, and Xu (詡) [the transcribed sequence of names is uncertain]. His wife was née Cheng. He placed 120th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Tang, registered in a military household in Lizhou, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Shaonan, he was first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather was Lin; his father's name is illegible (□); and his mother was née Gan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shi, Yu, □, □, and Wei [the division of the illegible names is uncertain]. His wife was née Huang. He placed forty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Yingkui, registered in a military household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Jingxiang, he was sixth in birth order, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongwei; his grandfather was Chang; his father was Qi, a district magistrate; his mother was née He; and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fu; his younger brothers were Yingshen, Yingyi, Yingzhen, and Yingwei. His wife was née Lu. He placed eighty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shilong, registered in a military household in Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhongxiu, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ben; his grandfather was Tong, a student of the Directorate of Education; his father was Lu; and his mother was née Zhu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Shisheng and Shibi. His wife was née Shi. He placed eighteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李時〔貫順天府涿州，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字孟□□一，年三十，十二月初五日生〕。曾祖奉，祖□□，父□□，母劉氏。具慶下，□□，妻史氏。順天府鄉試第□□名，會試第一百八十六名。

常道〔貫直隸鳳陽府滁州來安縣，軍籍，河南陳留縣人，來安縣學生，治易經，字文載，行二，年三十，九月二十一日生〕。曾祖全，祖智，父泰〔監生〕，母郝氏。永感下，兄經，弟教，娶蘇氏。應天府鄉試第二十八名，會試第一百五十五名。
translation_en:
Tu Yao 屠垚, registered in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Wenzhi, he ranked seventh in his family, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, posthumously granted the title of Minister of Justice; his grandfather was Zhen, posthumously granted the title of Judge; his father was Xi, a Vice Prefect; and his mother, née Lu, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kui, a Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his elder paternal cousins were Bi, Gui, and Hou; his younger brother was Ye; and his younger paternal cousins were Kai, Zhang (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Dian. He married a woman née Shen and subsequently a woman née Ni. He placed fifty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shi 李時, registered in Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name began with Meng, but the remaining text and apparent family ranking are damaged [?]. He was thirty years old, born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather’s and father’s names are illegible; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. A further detail is illegible [?]; his wife was née Shi. His rank in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination is illegible; he placed 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Hui 張惠, registered in Ninghai Subprefecture, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tianze, he ranked thirty-second in his family, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Quan, his father Tong, and his mother née Ma. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Song. He placed eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chang Dao 常道, registered in Lai’an County, Chuzhou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was originally from Chenliu County, Henan. He was a student of the Lai’an County school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Wenzai, he ranked second in his family, and he was thirty years old, born on the twenty-first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Quan, his grandfather Zhi, his father Tai (a student of the Directorate of Education), and his mother née Hao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jing and his younger brother Jiao. He married a woman née Su. He placed twenty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳琛〔貫福建漳州府龍溪縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字思獻，行二，年三十二，十月十二日生〕。曾祖溫義，祖實榮，父英，母歐氏。慈侍下，兄穆，弟樸，娶林氏。福建鄉試第三十三名，會試第一百六名。

熊泰〔貫湖廣武昌府武昌縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字元來，行二，年三十六，二月十八日生〕。曾祖悌，祖敬，父英，母方氏。永感下，兄春，娶周氏，繼娶朱氏。湖廣鄉試第十七名，會試第二百七十一名。
translation_en:
Li Ji 李楫, registered in Huaining County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jizhi; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight, born on the second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, Chief Physician; his grandfather was Sheng, Medical Instructor, posthumously appointed Assistant Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; and his father was Jin, formerly a Prefect. His father’s former wife, née Xu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace (anren); his mother, née Geng, was granted the same title. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Gan, an honorary official for contributions to public welfare; his younger brothers were Qing, Tang, Fei, and Dong. He married a woman née Zu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Mengju 孫孟舉, registered in Shanghe County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guozhi; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-three, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, posthumously appointed Magistrate; his grandfather was Cheng, posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Shi, a Prefect. His father’s former wife, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability (yiren); his mother, also née Zhang, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mengzong and Minxue; his younger brother was Menghe, a Metropolitan Examination graduate (gongshi). He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Chen 陳琛, registered in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Sixian; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-two, born on the twelfth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenyi, his grandfather Shirong, his father Ying, and his mother a woman née Ou. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Mu and his younger brother Pu. He married a woman née Lin. He placed thirty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Tai 熊泰, registered in Wuchang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanlai; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-six, born on the eighteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ti, his grandfather Jing, his father Ying, and his mother a woman née Fang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Chun. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Zhu. He placed seventeenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tian Ruzi 田汝耔, courtesy name Qinfu, was registered in an artisan household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third among his brothers, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deng; his grandfather, Mao; and his father, An, an Assistant Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Yang, and his mother was née Wei. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rugeng and Ruyun, and his younger brothers were Rusi, Runou, and Ruyou. His wife was née Tao. He ranked sixty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Kuan 張寬, courtesy name Deli, was registered in a military household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first among his brothers, aged thirty-two, and born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng, an honorary official; his grandfather, Da, a Clerk; his father, Jing; and his mother, née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Chong, and his wife was née Zhou. He ranked fifty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xiao 劉孝, courtesy name Bida, was registered in a civilian household in Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first among his brothers, aged thirty-seven, and born on the thirtieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingwen; his grandfather, Zheng; and his father, Kui, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Zhang, held the title Lady of Virtue. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brother was Benli. He married a woman née Fan and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He ranked twentieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Teng Ji 滕紀, courtesy name Zizhen, was registered with the Front Guard of the Palace Garrison, with the registration category unclear [?], and was a native of Laiyang County, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second among his brothers, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhou; his grandfather, Sheng; his father, Jun; and his mother, née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Gang. He married a woman née Su and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gu Xuan 顧瑄, courtesy name Yuqing, was registered in a banner household of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Pinghu County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather Jing and father Rong were company commanders. His mother was née Yu, and his stepmother née Niu; both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Zhang, a company commander, Zan, Huan, and Tang. He married a woman née Gao. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Jin 陶金, courtesy name Chunfu, was registered in an official household in Tianchang County, Sizhou, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Xuan, a county magistrate; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Sui, and he married a woman née Chen. He ranked ninety-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhe 吳哲, courtesy name Ziming, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongyu [annotation illegible: □□], his grandfather’s name is illegible (□□), and his father was Xuan. His legal mother was née Yang, and his birth mother née Zhou. Both parents were living. The names of his elder brothers are transcribed as 啓□唐周□ [?], and those of his younger brothers as 吉評語㪍問 [?]; the individual names cannot be reliably distinguished. He married a woman née Shan. He ranked thirty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Lei 曹雷, courtesy name Qidong, was registered in a military household in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, and was a native of Taizhou in the directly administered metropolitan region. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Er, his grandfather Hui, an honorary official, and his father Shu; his mother was née Ge. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lin, an honorary official, and Bin; his younger brothers were Zhen and Yun. He married a woman née Guo. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Pan Xuan 潘選, registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuxuan. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Risheng; his grandfather, Sixin; his father, Jie, an Imperial Academy student; and his mother, née Qi. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yu, and his wife was née Hu. He ranked sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Fu 楊輔, registered in a civilian household in Pizhou, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jieqing. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-one and was born on the thirteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Li, a District Magistrate; his father, Zan; his mother, née Xiao; and his stepmother, née Liu. Grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Lu, Che, Lin, Lun, and Shi, and his wife was née Chen. He ranked 131st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Shanfu 鄭善夫, registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an added-quota student of the Houguan County school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jizhi. Sixth in birth order, he was aged twenty-one and was born on the twentieth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Keng; his grandfather, Shu; his father, Yuanli; and his mother, née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fengchun; his younger brothers were Fengtai, Fenggao, Fengdong, and Fengnan. His wife was née Yuan. He ranked forty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Bangqi 張邦奇, registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Changfu. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-two and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather, Chen; his father, Shimin, an honorary official; and his mother, née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Bangyan; his younger brothers were Bangyan 邦言, Bangliang, Bangjun, Bangyi, Bangjie, Bangheng, Bangzhi, and Bangyong. His wife was née Wang. He ranked fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zeng Nian was registered in a military household in Yongxing County, Chenzhou, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Shengchu and was seventh in family order, aged forty, born on the fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Rubai; his grandfather, Keqian, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Beng 䭰 [?], was a Prefect; and his mother, née Chu, held the title Lady of Repose. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qi, an honorary official; Jie; Yu; Tong, formerly a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and Qian, an honorary official. He married a woman née Deng. He placed thirteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Deng was registered in a civilian household in Chang'an County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Younian and was second in family order, aged twenty-seven, born on the thirtieth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Wentong, his grandfather was Rong, and his father was Huaiqian. Two mothers are listed, née Xiao and née Dang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yuan. He married a woman née Fan. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Da was registered in a military household of the Chuzhou Guard [?], Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name □□ and was second in family order, aged thirty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Jingcheng, his grandfather was Xiangfang, his father was Zongtai, and his mother was née Hou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hong, a District Magistrate, and □, an Assistant Instructor; his younger brother was Tong. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Pan. He placed seventy-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yuan was registered in an official household of the Zhuolu Left Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Deshen and was third in family order, aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Su, and grandfather, Yu, each held the title General of Illustrious Courage and served as a Guard Commander. His father was Guang, and his mother was née Jue. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hao, who likewise held the title General of Illustrious Courage and served as a Guard Commander, and Run; his younger brothers were Pu, Ru, Han, Tan, Zi, and Ze. He married a woman née Guo. He placed thirty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Dunfu, his grandfather Yin, and his father Shouxin; his mother was née Gao and his stepmother née Xu; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Deguang, Deyue, and Defeng, his wife was née Peng, and he placed fifteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Shufang, his grandfather’s name and accompanying annotation are illegible [?], his father was Tingbi, an official of yin-yang studies, and his mother was née Zhai; both parents were living, the following three characters are illegible [?], his wife was née Ma, and he placed sixty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Zijia [annotation illegible], his grandfather Rixiu [annotation illegible], his father Qiangang, and his mother née Fang; his parents and at least one grandparent were living, his elder brother Ximeng was a tribute scholar (gongshi), his younger brothers Xishao, Xiyong, and Xihuo were all government school students, his wife was née Lin, and he placed forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Jing, registered in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yizhong, he ranked thirty-second among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the seventeenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Keyong, his grandfather Degao, his father Wenzhi, and his mother née Yang; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Pu, his younger brothers were Jie, Ting, Zan, and Qi, his wife was née Yang, and he placed sixty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

His courtesy name was Yunsheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Rang, and his father Lun; his mother was née Wu and his stepmother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Shi and Bao, and his wife was née He. He placed seventeenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zan, registered in a civilian household in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His great-grandfather was Yongbin, his grandfather Yongming, and his father Xian; his mother was née Cheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Yi, E, and Fang, and his wife was née Huang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhongxian, registered in a civilian household in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was an added-quota student at the Tang County Confucian school in Zhili, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shangde; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiaoxian, his grandfather Ben, and his father Tong; his mother was née Tang (湯) and his stepmother née Jia. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhongliang, and his wife was née Tang (唐). He placed eighteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Cunzhi, registered in a civilian household in Taikang County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruyu; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Ji, and his father En; his mother was née Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Cunli. He married a woman née Zhao and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Kong. He placed sixty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and three hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Yang, registered in Xinyang Guard, Henan, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Wangzhi. He ranked tenth among his brothers and was twenty-three years old, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, a Battalion Commander; his grandfather, Sheng, a Vice Commander; and his father, Shan, a Commander. His legal mother was née Yuan, and his birth mother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin, a Commander, Can, Chao, and Pei; his younger brothers were Jiang, Yi, Ze, and Shu. He married a woman née He. He placed twenty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Fang, registered in Zhenjiang Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Dantu County school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruxue. He ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhou; his grandfather, Rong; his father, Shou; and his mother, née Lü. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brothers were Xiao and Ru. He married a woman née Yu. He placed twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Mi, courtesy name Deyi, was registered in a civilian household in Changping County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Huairen County, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fifth in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Qing was Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial; his grandfather Sheng was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), granted the honorary title of Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his father Dao was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his mother, née Han, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yu, Shoude [?] (a squad leader in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard authorized to wear the official cap and sash), and Huan. He married a woman née Cao and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed twenty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wei, courtesy name Shiyuan, was registered in a military household in Jimo County, Jiaozhou Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhiyan; his grandfather Rong was a County Vice Magistrate; his father Ji was a tribute student (gongshi); and his mother was née Shao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Ren, and his younger brothers were Shen, Shi, and Ru. He married a woman née Liu. He placed seventeenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Ying, courtesy name Ziqian, was registered in a military household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked 108th in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Siwen had received an official commendation as a righteous commoner; his grandfather was Kongshou; his father was Yu; and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhi, Wu, and Zhu, and his younger brothers were Lang and Gai. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Gui, courtesy name Daochong, was registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yancai; his grandfather was Yingmao; and his father was Bin. His father's former wife was née Li, his mother was née Gao, and his stepmother was née Zeng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rong, and his younger brothers were Xian (a tribute student, gongshi), Neng, Shun, and Kuan. He married a woman née Li. He placed forty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Yao 王瑶, registered in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes (Shijing). His courtesy name was Peizhi, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather, Wen, was a prefectural records examiner; and his father, Ji, was an instructor. His mother was née Zhu. His mother alone was living. His younger brother was Lian. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently women née Xun and née Cai. He placed fifty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Song 章嵩, registered in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes (Shijing). His courtesy name was Shizhan, and he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boyang; his grandfather, Shanliang; and his father, Zhonghua. His mother was née Dong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Mao, and his younger brothers were Chun, Rui, Qin, Bang, and Huang. He married a woman née Wen. He placed twenty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

text:

之序亦有相須而

Now, among emperors, none surpassed Yao and Shun in sagehood; among kings, none surpassed …

text:
禹湯文武致治之
盛萬世如見其為
道為法之跡具載
諸經可考而證之
乎自是而降若漢
===
若唐若宋賢明之
君所以創業於前
而守成於後是道
是法亦未嘗有外
焉何治效之終不

title: 弘治十八年進士登科錄
text:
能古若乎我
聖祖高皇帝定天下
之初建極垂憲
列聖相承益隆繼述
為道為法蓋與古
===
帝王之聖先後一
揆矣朕自莅祚以
來夙夜兢兢圖光
先烈于兹有年然而
治效未臻其極豈

translation_en: …equal those of antiquity? When Our Sagely Progenitor, the Emperor Gao, first pacified All Under Heaven, he established the supreme standard and handed down laws. The successive sage emperors carried on his legacy, further advancing and developing his work. Their principles and institutions surely accorded with those of the sage emperors and kings of antiquity, following the same standard across the ages. Since ascending the throne, I have been vigilant and circumspect morning and night, seeking to bring glory to the illustrious achievements of my predecessors, for many years now. Yet the results of government have not reached their highest excellence. Could it be that…

title: 弘治十八年進士登科錄
text:
於是道有未行是
法有未守乎抑雖
行之守之而尚未
盡若古乎子諸生
明經積學究心當
===
世之務必有定見
其直述以對毋徒
騁浮辭而不切實
用朕將采而行之

===

punctuated: 於是道有未行，是法有未守乎？抑雖行之守之，而尚未盡若古乎？子諸生明經積學，究心當世之務，必有定見，其直述以對，毋徒騁浮辭而不切實用。朕將采而行之。
translation_en: …have these principles not been put into practice, or these models not been observed? Or, although they have been practiced and observed, have we still fallen short of fully matching antiquity? You students have mastered the Classics, accumulated learning, and devoted your minds to the affairs of the present age; you must have considered views. State them plainly in your replies. Do not merely indulge in empty rhetoric that has no bearing on practical use. I shall adopt your proposals and put them into effect.

title: 弘治十八年進士登科錄
text:
臣顧鼎臣
臣對臣聞帝王有治天下之大體有治天下
之大用體者何道是也用者何法是也道根
於心法之所由立也法施於政道之所由行
也法而非道則所以主張之者無其本道而
非法則所以經綸之者無其具皆非所以治
天下也然有是道則其法可立未有善立是
法而不本於道者也有是法則其道可行未
有能行其道而不知守乎法者也道行而無
弊法立而能守則推之無不準動之無不化
外無不攘內無不安遠無不至邇無不服端
拱於九重之上而操縱翕張所向如意運用
於四海之間而渾融貫徹所在歸極尚何治
之不古若哉帝之所以帝王之所以王我
皇祖之所以創造
列聖之所以繼述皆不外此彼漢唐宋者道非其
道法非其法又何恠乎治效之不能比隆於
唐虞三代也哉欽惟
皇帝陛下天啟
聖神日新

臣對：臣聞帝王有治天下之大體，有治天下之大用。體者何？道是也。用者何？法是也。道根於心，法之所由立也；法施於政，道之所由行也。法而非道，則所以主張之者無其本；道而非法，則所以經綸之者無其具，皆非所以治天下也。然有是道，則其法可立，未有善立是法而不本於道者也；有是法，則其道可行，未有能行其道而不知守乎法者也。道行而無弊，法立而能守，則推之無不準，動之無不化；外無不攘，內無不安，遠無不至，邇無不服。端拱於九重之上，而操縱翕張，所向如意；運用於四海之間，而渾融貫徹，所在歸極。尚何治之不古若哉？帝之所以帝，王之所以王，我皇祖之所以創造，列聖之所以繼述，皆不外此。彼漢唐宋者，道非其道，法非其法，又何恠乎治效之不能比隆於唐虞三代也哉？欽惟皇帝陛下，天啟聖神，日新
translation_en:
Your servant, Gu Dingchen.
Your servant replies: I have heard that emperors and kings possess both the fundamental substance and the great practical instruments for governing All under Heaven. What is this substance? It is the Way. What are these instruments? They are laws and institutions. The Way is rooted in the heart: it is that upon which laws and institutions are established. Laws and institutions are applied in government: they are that through which the Way is put into practice. With laws and institutions but without the Way, what sustains them lacks its foundation; with the Way but without laws and institutions, what orders the realm lacks its instruments. Neither suffices to govern All under Heaven. Yet when this Way is present, its laws and institutions can be established; no one has ever established them well without grounding them in the Way. When these laws and institutions are present, the Way can be practiced; no one has ever practiced the Way without knowing how to uphold them. If the Way is practiced without abuses and laws and institutions are established and upheld, then wherever they are extended they accord with the proper standard, and wherever they are set in motion they bring transformation. Abroad, no threat remains unrepelled; at home, none remain unsettled. Their influence reaches all who are distant, and all who are near submit. Sitting upright with hands folded in the innermost palace, the ruler controls and releases, contracts and expands, accomplishing his wishes in every direction. Exercising his rule throughout the Four Seas, he achieves an integrated and all-pervading order, with all places turning toward the supreme standard. How, then, could his government fail to equal that of antiquity? This is what made the ancient emperors emperors and the ancient kings kings; it is what enabled our imperial ancestor to found the dynasty and the successive sage sovereigns to carry forward his work. None went beyond this. As for the Han, Tang, and Song, their Way was not that Way, and their laws and institutions were not those laws and institutions. Why, then, wonder that their achievements in government could not rival the flourishing rule of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties?
I reverently consider that Your Majesty the Emperor possesses Heaven-endowed sagacity and spiritual insight, daily renewing…

title: 弘治十八年進士登科錄
text:
德學大化神明洽于遠邇至治馨香徹于上下
所謂學于古訓而有獲監于成憲而無愆者
盖卓卓乎足以光
前而裕後矣茲者開賢科擢多士
御大廷降
明詔猶謂治效未臻其極而拳拳以行道守法
為問臣雖至陋寧不鼓舞感動思罄愚衷以
對揚
休命乎竊惟天生萬物不能自理而命之聖人
故曰天佑下民作之君作之師惟其克相上
===
帝寵綏四方夫以一人之身加于兆民之上
而付之以君師治教之責亦大且難矣求盡
是責以無負乎天之所命舍道與法二者其
奚以哉是故脩身齊家治國平天下治之道
也道者治之體也建立紀綱分正百職順天
揆事創制立度以盡天下之務治之法也法
者道之用也甞考朱熹之訓曰道猶路也法
法度也董仲舒亦曰道者所由適於治之路
也謂之路則可見其為人之所共由謂之度
則可見其為人之所當守是二者理與事有
